# django-vantage

> A smart, beautiful admin panel for Django. Zero config to start, one line to override anything.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/

<div class="dv-hero" markdown>

# A smart, beautiful admin panel for Django

<p class="dv-tagline">Zero config to start. One line to override anything.
Install it, and every model you have is already administrable — with a data grid,
charts, a command palette, light and dark themes and a schema map.</p>

[Get started](getting-started.md){ .md-button .md-button--primary }
[View on GitHub](https://github.com/Pythondeveloper6/django-vantage){ .md-button }

</div>

![The Orders list in django-vantage: stat cards, a revenue chart, a status breakdown and a filtered data grid](assets/screenshots/orders-light.webp){ .dv-shot .dv-only-light }
![The Orders list in django-vantage, dark theme](assets/screenshots/orders-dark.webp){ .dv-shot .dv-only-dark }

!!! warning "Beta — `0.3.0b1`"

    Feature-complete for its scope and heavily tested — more than 5,000 tests. The API is stable apart from items marked provisional, and changes go through a [deprecation cycle](api-stability.md).
    See the [FAQ](faq.md#how-finished-is-this) for an honest account of what is and is
    not done. Use it on an internal tool; pin the exact version if you depend on it.

## Sixty seconds

```bash
pip install --pre django-vantage
```

```python
# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = ["vantage", ...]
```

```python
# urls.py
from django.urls import path
from vantage import site

urlpatterns = [path("admin/", site.urls)]
```

That is the whole setup. Every model in the project is now administrable.

To change one model, write a `panel.py` next to its `models.py`:

```python
from vantage import ModelPanel, register

from blog.models import Post


@register(Post)
class PostPanel(ModelPanel):
    list_display = ["title", "author", "status", "published_at"]  # (1)!
```

1.  Only the columns change. Filters, search fields and widgets stay inferred —
    partial configuration never opts you out of the rest.

Not sure what was inferred? Ask the package to write it down:

```bash
python manage.py vantage_scaffold blog
```

That prints a real `panel.py` containing exactly what Vantage decided. Own it, edit it,
or delete an attribute to hand it back to inference.
Full walkthrough: [Getting started](getting-started.md).
Want the whole list in one place? [Features at a glance](features.md).

## What you get

<div class="grid cards" markdown>

-   :material-auto-fix:{ .lg .middle } **Inferred, attribute by attribute**

    ---

    Columns, filters, search, sort order, widgets and query optimisation come from the
    model itself. Override one and the rest stay inferred.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Inference](inference.md)

-   :material-table-large:{ .lg .middle } **A real data grid**

    ---

    Saved views, grouping, density, column picker, inline editing, trash and restore,
    bulk actions that scale to "select all 40,000 matching".

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Lists](lists.md)

-   :material-chart-areaspline:{ .lg .middle } **Stats and charts in Python**

    ---

    `Stat` and `Chart` declared on the panel, computed on the filtered rows, folded
    into as few queries as possible. Inline SVG — no JavaScript.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Analytics](analytics.md)

-   :material-form-select:{ .lg .middle } **Forms with a layout DSL**

    ---

    `Tabs`, `Section` and `Row`; editable inlines; a cascade-delete preview that
    shows the real tree of what goes with a record.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Forms](forms.md)

-   :material-shield-lock-outline:{ .lg .middle } **Permissions that hold**

    ---

    Three layers, enforced on every view, bulk action and API call. Read-only mode
    and impersonation live in the permission layer; multi-tenancy is fail-closed.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Permissions](permissions.md)

-   :material-api:{ .lg .middle } **A JSON API for free**

    ---

    Every panel, through the same permission and validation path as the UI, with
    cursor pagination and optimistic concurrency.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: The JSON API](api.md)

-   :material-palette-outline:{ .lg .middle } **One colour, a whole theme**

    ---

    A brand colour becomes a complete light and dark palette with contrast checked.
    RTL from day one.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Theming](theming.md)

-   :material-view-column-outline:{ .lg .middle } **Board, calendar, gallery, map**

    ---

    Any list as a Kanban board, a month calendar, a gallery or a map — inferred from
    the model, with the grouping field picked from the page.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: List views](list-views.md)

-   :material-undo-variant:{ .lg .middle } **Undo**

    ---

    Deletes, bulk edits and inline edits offer an Undo toast, and never restore over
    somebody else's newer change.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Undo](undo.md)

-   :material-eye-off-outline:{ .lg .middle } **Secrets masked by default**

    ---

    Passwords, tokens and card numbers are hidden everywhere, revealed one at a time
    by people allowed to, and every reveal is logged.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Sensitive fields](sensitive-fields.md)

-   :material-account-key-outline:{ .lg .middle } **Roles and data quality**

    ---

    A permission matrix for Django groups, and a read-only audit of the data in every
    model.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Roles](roles.md) · [Data quality](data-quality.md)

-   :material-tune-variant:{ .lg .middle } **Configurable from the UI too**

    ---

    Columns, filters, stats, the dashboard, the sidebar and the branding — without a
    deploy, in one fixed order with `panel.py`.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: How configuration resolves](configuration.md)

</div>

## The two rules

Everything in this package follows from two rules.

**1. Smart.** Install it, and every model in your project already has a usable admin.
Columns, filters, search fields, sort order, widgets and query optimisation are all
inferred from the model itself. You write no configuration to get something worth
looking at.

**2. Easy.** Every inferred default is overridable in one line, and overriding one
thing overrides only that thing. Setting `list_display` changes the columns; your
filters, search and widgets stay inferred. Partial configuration never opts you out of
the rest of the intelligence.

The second rule is the load-bearing one. A tool where "customise anything" means
"customise everything" gets abandoned the first time someone needs one different
column. Inference is therefore resolved **per attribute**, not as a single
all-or-nothing fallback — see [Inference](inference.md).

**A developer's API is not the only person who has to configure this.** Whatever you
can set in `panel.py` or `VANTAGE`, the person running the panel day to day can often
set from the UI instead — a list's columns and filters, the branding, the behaviour —
without a deploy, and without your Python file becoming a fiction of what actually
renders. The two ways compose in one fixed order, stated once: see
[How configuration resolves](configuration.md).

## Requirements

Python 3.12+ and Django 5.2+ (including 6.x). Django is the only runtime dependency.
No Node.js — the CSS and JavaScript ship prebuilt and depend on nothing.
django-guardian, django-rules, django-mptt, django-treebeard and
django-simple-history are all used when present and never required.

# Features at a glance

Everything django-vantage does, one short paragraph each, with a link to the full page.
Unless it says otherwise, a feature works the moment the package is installed: nothing
here needs configuring before you can use it.

## Getting set up

**Auto-registration.** Add `vantage` to `INSTALLED_APPS`, mount `site.urls`, and every
model in the project gets a list, detail, create, edit and delete page. Framework noise
(sessions, content types, permissions) is left out. [Getting started](getting-started.md)

**Inference.** Columns, filters, search fields, sort order, form widgets and query
joins are worked out from each model. Set one attribute on a panel and only that
attribute changes; the rest stay inferred. [Inference](inference.md)

**Panels.** A `panel.py` next to `models.py` holds the overrides, in ordinary Python with
names a `ModelAdmin` user already knows (`list_display`, `search_fields`,
`readonly_fields`…). [Panels](panels.md)

**`vantage_scaffold`.** Prints a real `panel.py` containing everything that was inferred,
so you can see the decisions and take ownership of any of them.
[See what was inferred](getting-started.md#see-what-was-inferred)

**`manage.py check`.** Every field name in a panel is validated at check time, so a typo
fails loudly instead of quietly dropping a column.
[Check your configuration](getting-started.md#check-your-configuration)

**Configure from the UI too.** Columns, filters, stats, the dashboard, the sidebar and the
branding can also be changed in the panel without a deploy. One fixed order decides who
wins: UI override, then `panel.py` / `VANTAGE`, then inference.
[How configuration resolves](configuration.md)

## Lists

**Data grid.** Sortable columns, a filter rail with counts, relative date filters
("last 30 days"), full-text search and pagination. [Lists](lists.md)

**Board, calendar, gallery and map.** The same list as a Kanban board, a month calendar,
an image gallery or a map, picked from a switcher. Each view is inferred from the model,
and **Group by** / **Dates from** let anyone choose the field from the page.
[List views](list-views.md)

**Saved views.** Save a combination of filters, search, sort and view under a name, keep
it private or share it. [Saved views](lists.md#saved-views)

**Inline editing.** Edit chosen columns in the grid. Changes collect in a pending bar and
are saved together in one transaction, with a conflict check if someone else changed the
row. [Inline cell editing](lists.md#inline-cell-editing)

**Grouping, trees and trash.** Group rows by a field, browse tree-shaped models, and get a
Trash tab with Restore on any model with a `deleted_at` or `is_deleted` column.
[Grouping, trees and trash](lists.md#grouping-trees-and-trash)

**Bulk actions.** Decorate a panel method with `@action` and it appears on the list.
"Select all matching" works on forty thousand rows as cheaply as on three, and big jobs
can run in the background. [Bulk actions](lists.md#bulk-actions)

**Undo.** Deletes, bulk edits and inline edits show a toast with an **Undo** button for a
few seconds. Nothing is ever restored over somebody else's newer change. [Undo](undo.md)

**History.** See any record as it was on a given date, replayed from the audit log, and
restore some or all of its fields. Fields the log cannot vouch for are labelled, never
guessed. [History](history.md)

**Approvals.** `requires_approval = ["price", "status"]` makes a change to those fields
wait for someone with permission to approve it; the rest of the edit saves as usual.
A request is never applied over a newer value. [Approvals](approvals.md)

**Export and import.** CSV, TSV, JSON, Excel and PDF export of exactly what you are looking at, and a
CSV import wizard that maps, previews and validates before writing anything.
[Export](lists.md#export) · [Import](lists.md#import)

**Customise a list from the page.** The Customise rail lets a person reorder and hide
columns, pick filters and add stats for themselves, or for everyone if they may.
[The customisation rail](lists.md#the-customisation-rail)

## Numbers and charts

**Summary bar.** A footer that sums money columns, averages ratings and leaves
identifiers alone, with no configuration. [The summary bar](analytics.md#the-summary-bar)

**Stats and charts.** Declare `Stat` and `Chart` on a panel; they follow the current
filters, compare against the previous period, and render as inline SVG.
[Analytics](analytics.md)

**Dashboard.** Stat, chart, table and list cards declared in Python, or built and
rearranged from the UI. [Dashboards](pages-and-dashboards.md#dashboards)

## Records and forms

**Inferred forms.** Widgets chosen per field type — searchable pickers for big relations,
a colour picker, image thumbnails, a JSON editor — grouped into sections.
[Forms](forms.md)

**Layout DSL.** `Tabs`, `Tab`, `Section` and `Row` arrange the form when the inferred
grouping is not what you want. [The layout DSL](forms.md#the-layout-dsl)

**Editable inlines.** Edit child records on the parent's page, in one transaction.
[Editable inlines](forms.md#editable-inlines)

**Duplicate and bulk edit.** Both reuse exactly the form and validation a single record
uses. [Duplicating a record](forms.md#duplicating-a-record) ·
[Bulk edit](forms.md#bulk-edit)

**Cascade-delete preview.** Before a delete, see everything it takes with it, counted.
[Cascade-delete preview](forms.md#cascade-delete-preview)

**History.** Every change made through the panel is in the record's history, with a diff.
[The audit log](permissions.md#the-audit-log)

## Access and safety

**Permissions.** Django's model permissions out of the box, with object-level and row
filtering hooks, enforced on every page, action and API call. django-guardian and
django-rules are picked up if installed. [Permissions](permissions.md)

**Roles.** Manage Django groups as roles in a permission matrix: tick view / add /
change / delete per model, review the diff, save once. Nobody can grant a permission they
do not hold. [Roles](roles.md)

**Sensitive fields.** Fields named like `password`, `api_token`, `iban` or `card_number`
are masked everywhere — lists, exports, search, the API, the audit log. A permitted user
can reveal one value at a time, and each reveal is logged. [Sensitive fields](sensitive-fields.md)

**Read-only mode.** One setting turns every write off, for a maintenance window or a
replica. [Read-only mode](permissions.md#read-only-mode)

**Impersonation.** See the panel as another user, with a banner you cannot miss.
[Impersonation](permissions.md#impersonation)

**Audit log.** Who changed what, when, from where, with a diff.
[The audit log](permissions.md#the-audit-log)

**Multi-tenancy.** Scope every model to the current tenant with one setting. Anything it
cannot scope is refused, not shown. [Multi-tenancy](tenancy.md)

**Security hardening.** Login throttling, CSP nonces, upload validation and `--deploy`
checks. [Security](security.md)

## Look and feel

**Brand colour.** One colour becomes a full light and dark palette, contrast-checked.
Logo, title and theme can also be set from the settings screen. [Theming](theming.md)

**Theme presets.** Pick a whole look — `vantage`, `shadcn`, `slate`, `rose` and more — in
one line, and let each person choose their own from the account page.
[UI theme presets](ui-themes.md)

**A layout for phones.** Lists become cards, bulk actions a bottom sheet, navigation a
drawer. [Phones](phones.md)

**Light, dark and system.** With no flash on load. [Light, dark and system](theming.md#light-dark-and-system)

**Right to left and translations.** RTL layouts and English and Arabic catalogues ship
in the box. [Internationalization](internationalization.md)

**Environment banner.** A coloured banner so nobody mistakes production for staging.
[The environment banner](theming.md#the-environment-banner)

**Accessibility.** Keyboard navigation, labelled controls and visible focus throughout.
[Accessibility](accessibility.md)

## Getting around

**Command palette.** <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> jumps to any model, record, page or action.
[The command palette](pages-and-dashboards.md#the-command-palette)

**Global search.** Search across every model you can see, from the top bar.
[Global search](lists.md#global-search)

**Sidebar.** Group, rename, reorder and hide entries with `VANTAGE["NAV"]`, or from the UI.
A nav entry can hide a model, never grant access to one. [Settings reference](settings.md)

**Schema map.** A live diagram of your models and how they relate, every box a link.
[The built-in pages](pages-and-dashboards.md#the-built-in-pages)

## Operations

**Data quality.** A read-only audit of every model for empty fields, duplicate candidates,
broken references and odd dates. `manage.py vantage_data_quality --fail-on warn` runs the
same audit in CI. [Data quality](data-quality.md)

**System page.** Migrations, cache, database and task backend at a glance.
[The system page](deployment.md#the-system-page)

**Query-count guarantees.** Joins are derived from what each page renders, and tests
assert the number of queries does not grow with the number of rows.
[Query cost](lists.md#query-cost)

## Extending it

**Custom pages.** A class with a title and a `get_context` method becomes a page with a
URL and a nav entry. [Custom pages](pages-and-dashboards.md#custom-pages)

**Slots.** Put your own HTML into named places in the shell.
[Slots](extending.md#slots)

**Plugins.** A package can add panels, pages and widgets through an entry point.
[Plugins](extending.md#plugins)

**JSON API.** Every panel as a JSON API, through the same permission and validation path
as the UI. [The JSON API](api.md)

**`contrib.admin` adapter.** Existing `admin.py` files can be served by Vantage.
[The contrib.admin adapter](extending.md#the-contribadmin-adapter)

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/getting-started/

# Getting started

[← Index](index.md)

## Install

```bash
pip install --pre django-vantage
```

`--pre` is needed while Vantage is in beta: pip skips pre-releases unless asked. Pin
the exact version (`django-vantage==0.3.0b1`) if you depend on it, because provisional
items may still change before 1.0.

Python 3.12+ and Django 5.2, 6.0 or 6.1 are required. The only other package is `nh3`, the
HTML sanitiser behind [rich-text fields](rich-text.md); it installs by itself as a
prebuilt wheel, so there is nothing to compile.

## Mount it

Two edits to your project.

```python
# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    "django.contrib.auth",
    "django.contrib.contenttypes",
    "django.contrib.sessions",
    "django.contrib.messages",
    "django.contrib.staticfiles",
    "vantage",
    # your apps
]
```

```python
# urls.py
from django.urls import path
from vantage import site

urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", site.urls),
]
```

Vantage stores four things of its own — site configuration, an audit log, saved views
and per-list preferences — so run its migrations:

```bash
python manage.py migrate
```

Every one of those tables is optional in practice: if the table is missing, the layer
that uses it silently falls back to what the code says. That is deliberate, because a
settings layer that raises when its own table is absent makes the migration that would
create the table impossible to run. But you want the tables, so run `migrate`.

### Signing in

The panel redirects anonymous visitors to `settings.LOGIN_URL` and requires `is_staff`.

Vantage ships styled sign-in, sign-out and change-password views, because a panel that
hands a visitor an unstyled Django form has broken its own promise on the first screen
anyone ever sees:

```python
# urls.py
from django.urls import include, path
from vantage import site

urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", site.urls),
    path("accounts/", include("vantage.authviews")),
]
```

```python
# settings.py
LOGIN_URL = "/accounts/login/"
LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL = "/admin/"
```

The route names deliberately match `django.contrib.auth.urls` — `login`, `logout`,
`password_change` — and no `app_name` is declared, so it is a drop-in replacement:
`LOGIN_URL`, `redirect_to_login` and every `{% url 'login' %}` in your project keep
working unchanged. Swap the include back for `django.contrib.auth.urls` at any time.

Add [`LOGIN_IMAGE`](settings.md#branding) for a two-column sign-in page.

Vantage also provides 403, 404 and 500 handlers that render inside the panel shell,
with a bare fallback for when the shell itself cannot render.

## First look

Start the server and open `/admin/`. Without a line of configuration you have:

- a **dashboard** with a count card per model you can see, a chart of new records over
  time, and a recent-records table for each model that stamps a creation date;
- a **list page** per model, with inferred columns, a filter rail, a search box, sortable
  headers, a per-column summary bar and CSV/TSV/NDJSON export;
- **create, edit and delete** pages, with widgets inferred from the field types and a
  cascade-delete preview that counts what a delete would take with it;
- a **command palette** on <kbd>⌘K</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, with global search across
  every model you have permission to open;
- a **schema map** at `/admin/_/schema/`, derived from the registry so it cannot go
  stale;
- a **system page** at `/admin/_/health/` for superusers;
- **light, dark and system themes**, and right-to-left layout when the active language
  is RTL.

### What gets registered

Every concrete, non-abstract model in `INSTALLED_APPS` is registered automatically,
minus framework plumbing nobody wants to browse: sessions, content types,
`auth.Permission`, `admin.LogEntry` and Vantage's own tables. `auth.User` and
`auth.Group` are deliberately kept — they are among the most useful things to
administer.

Narrow it with [`EXCLUDE` or `INCLUDE_ONLY`](settings.md#discovery), or switch
auto-registration off entirely with `AUTO_REGISTER = False` and register by hand.

## Configure one model

Create `panel.py` next to `models.py` in any app. Vantage imports it automatically at
startup, the same way `django.contrib.admin` imports `admin.py`.

```python
# blog/panel.py
from vantage import ModelPanel, register

from blog.models import Post


@register(Post)
class PostPanel(ModelPanel):
    icon = "file-text"
    group = "Content"
    list_display = ["title", "author", "status", "published_at"]
```

That overrides the columns. Filters, search fields, sort order and every form widget
are still inferred. See [Panels](panels.md) for the full attribute list and
[Inference](inference.md) for what the defaults are.

## See what was inferred

Inference is only trustworthy if you can look at it. `vantage_scaffold` renders the
engine's decisions as the Python you would have written:

```bash
python manage.py vantage_scaffold shop
```

Running that against the demo project prints, among others:

```python
@register(Order)
class OrderPanel(ModelPanel):
    list_display = [
        "number",
        "status",
        "customer",
        "shipping_city",
        "total",
        "created_at",
    ]
    list_link = "number"
    list_filter = ["status", "created_at", "customer"]
    list_search = ["number", "shipping_city", "note", "customer__name"]
    ordering = ["-created_at"]
```

Two flags:

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--write` | Write `panel.py` into the app directory instead of printing it |
| `--force` | Overwrite an existing `panel.py` |

Once written, the file is ordinary code: readable in a diff, editable, and no longer
subject to inference changing under it on upgrade. Delete an attribute and it returns
to being inferred. Delete the whole file and the models stay registered.

## Check your configuration

Mistakes in a panel should fail at startup, not surface as a puzzling page.

```bash
python manage.py check
```

Vantage registers six system checks: one for the `VANTAGE` settings dict (unknown keys,
invalid choices), one for every registered panel (field paths that do not resolve, a
`list_link` outside `list_display`, a layout naming a field the model does not have),
one for the `NAV` declaration, one for [multi-tenancy](tenancy.md) (a model with no
path to the tenant and no exemption — fails closed, so this check exists to name every
model that would otherwise show nothing), one for plugins that failed to load, and one
for the `contrib.admin` adapter (settings an adopted `ModelAdmin` declared that could
not be translated). Panels left entirely at their inferred defaults are skipped — there
is no user-written configuration to be wrong.

A further set of checks only runs with `--deploy` — see [Security](security.md) and
[Deployment](deployment.md).

A typo in the settings dict is caught with a suggestion:

```
Unrecognised key(s) in the VANTAGE setting:
  'SITE_TTLE' is not a Vantage setting. Did you mean 'SITE_TITLE'?
```

## The demo project

The repository ships a complete demo — a small wholesale shop with seven models, two
hand-written panels and five left entirely alone, so you can compare them side by side.

```bash
./example/run.sh          # migrate, seed, and serve on :8765
```

Sign in as `admin` / `admin12345`.

`example/shop/panel.py` and `example/config/settings.py` are written to be read. They
are the shortest useful reference for most of what follows.

## Where next

- [Panels](panels.md) — every attribute you can set
- [Inference](inference.md) — what the defaults will be, and why
- [Lists](lists.md) — the list page in detail
- [Settings](settings.md) — project-wide configuration

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/configuration/

# How configuration resolves

[← Index](index.md)

This package has two ways to configure almost everything a panel does: write Python
(`panel.py` and the `VANTAGE` settings dict), or use the panel's own UI. They are not
two competing systems — they compose in one fixed order, and every page in this
documentation that has a UI layer links back to this one so the order only has to be
stated once.

> **UI override → `panel.py` / `VANTAGE` → inference.**
>
> The narrowest thing that has an opinion wins. A person using the panel can override
> what you wrote without touching a deploy; what you wrote in Python overrides what the
> package would otherwise have guessed; and the guess is always there as the floor, so
> a project that configures nothing still gets something worth looking at.

## Why it has to be this order, not some other one

Reverse the order — say, "Python always wins" — and the per-list customisation rail and
the settings screen stop being real features: a colleague hides a column at 9am, and it
reappears the moment anyone redeploys, because the code they never edited "wins". A UI
control that a redeploy can silently undo is not a control, it is a suggestion, and it
trains people to stop trusting it.

Reverse it the other way — "the UI always wins, permanently" — and `panel.py` stops
being the source of truth a developer can read to know what a page does. Six months of
UI tweaks by different people would leave a `list_display = [...]` in the repository
that nobody could relate to what actually renders, which is precisely the failure mode
a config-as-code tool exists to prevent.

So the rule is not "UI wins" or "Python wins" — it is **narrowest wins, and the
narrowest layer can always be reset back to what the code declares.** A UI override is
real and it is reversible, on purpose, by the same action: delete the override and you
are looking at `panel.py` again, not at a system nobody can fully explain.

## The same shape, wherever it appears

Every layer that stores a UI override follows the pattern
[`ListPreference`](lists.md#the-customisation-rail) established first: a database row
that sits **underneath** the getter a caller already uses, not beside it.

```python
def get_list_filter(self, request=None) -> list[str]:
    stored = listprefs.override(self, request, "list_filter")   # UI override
    if stored is not None:
        return list(stored)
    if self.list_filter is not None:                            # panel.py
        return list(self.list_filter)
    return inference.infer_list_filter(self.model)               # inference
```

Three consequences follow from writing it this way rather than as a single
all-or-nothing fallback:

- **Every existing call site picks up a UI override for free.** `check`, `scaffold`,
  the registry and a dashboard's table card all call `panel.get_list_display()` and
  none of them had to change when the UI layer was added — they simply keep asking the
  panel, and the panel now has one more place to check before it answers.
- **Resolution is per attribute, not per panel.** Overriding a list's columns from the
  UI does not switch off inference for its filters, and declaring `list_filter` in
  Python does not switch off the UI's ability to hide a column. Each getter runs its
  own three-step cascade independently — the same rule
  [Panels](panels.md#the-rule-that-governs-every-attribute) states for the Python layer
  alone, extended one layer further out.
- **The UI layer can only narrow, never widen.** A stored preference is checked against
  what the panel *currently* exposes, both when it is saved and again when it is read —
  see [the customisation rail's ceiling](lists.md#the-customisation-rail). A UI control
  that could show a column `panel.py` never declared would make the Python file a lie
  about what the page can do.

## "Why is my `panel.py` being ignored?"

One answer: **something narrower has an opinion.** In order:

1. **Is there a personal preference?** Open the surface's own UI control — the
   [customisation rail](lists.md#the-customisation-rail) on a list page, the
   [settings screen](theming.md#the-settings-screen) for branding and behaviour — and
   look for a "reset to what the code declares" action. If one is offered, something is
   currently overriding the code, by design.
2. **Is there a site-wide preference someone else saved?** Personal preferences apply
   only to the person who set them; a site-wide one applies to everyone and needs
   [`LIST_PREFS_PERMISSION`](settings.md#behaviour) or
   [`SETTINGS_PERMISSION`](settings.md#behaviour) to have been granted to set it. If you
   cannot see who changed it, that permission is too wide.
3. **Is the database table missing or unreachable?** Both layers are
   [failure-tolerant by design](faq.md#does-it-need-a-database-table) — a missing table
   resolves silently to whatever the code says, which means this is never the cause of
   a *wrong* value, only ever of a UI control quietly doing nothing. If the rail's
   changes are not sticking at all, check that `migrate` has run.
4. **Otherwise, it is inference filling a gap you thought you closed.** Confirm the
   attribute name is spelled the way `ModelPanel` expects — `manage.py check` catches a
   genuine typo, but an attribute that exists under a different name (`search_fields`
   vs. `list_search`, say) silently does nothing and inference answers instead. Run
   `manage.py vantage_scaffold <app>` to see what the panel currently resolves to and
   compare it against what you wrote.

Nothing in this list is "your Python was overruled by a bug" — every layer that can
override `panel.py` does so as its entire documented purpose, and every one of them
is reversible from the surface that set it.

## What is configurable from the UI today, and what is not

Not every knob has a UI layer yet. Sidebar navigation is Python-only for now: there is
no database-backed override for it, so `VANTAGE["NAV"]` is the only word on it, and
there is nothing to reset because nothing can be overridden. Everything else in the
table below — including the dashboard — has one.

| Surface | UI layer | Python layer | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|
| List columns, filters, search, stats, charts, summary bar | [The customisation rail](lists.md#the-customisation-rail), per list | `list_display`, `list_filter`, `list_search`, `list_stats`, `list_charts`, `list_aggregates` on `ModelPanel` | [Lists](lists.md), [Panels](panels.md) |
| Dashboard cards: which show, their order and width, and cards built entirely in the UI over any model | [`?arrange=1`](pages-and-dashboards.md#arranging-the-dashboard-from-the-ui) on the dashboard itself | `VANTAGE["DASHBOARD"]`, a `Dashboard` subclass | [Pages and dashboards](pages-and-dashboards.md#dashboards) |
| Branding: title, logo, favicon, brand colour, corner radius, theme | [The settings screen](theming.md#the-settings-screen) | `SITE_TITLE`, `LOGO`, `BRAND_COLOR`… in `VANTAGE` | [Theming](theming.md) |
| Behaviour: environment banner, rows per page, command palette, read-only mode | [The settings screen](theming.md#the-settings-screen) | `ENVIRONMENT`, `DEFAULT_PER_PAGE`, `COMMAND_PALETTE`, `READ_ONLY` in `VANTAGE` | [Settings](settings.md#behaviour) |
| Sidebar navigation: groups, order, labels, icons, hidden items, extra links | [The settings screen's Sidebar card](theming.md#the-settings-screen) | `VANTAGE["NAV"]` | [Settings](settings.md#navigation) |
| Permissions, tenancy | — Python only, deliberately: a permission boundary is not a preference | `VANTAGE["PERMISSIONS"]`, per-panel hooks, `VANTAGE["TENANT_MODEL"]` | [Permissions](permissions.md), [Multi-tenancy](tenancy.md) |

The bottom row is not an oversight to apologise for: a permission boundary that a
signed-in user could loosen from inside the panel would not be a boundary, and CSRF
tokens aside, "everyone who can reach the settings screen can also decide who can
delete records" is a sentence that should make you uneasy on sight. That one is
Python-only on purpose and will stay that way; the sidebar is Python-only simply
because a UI for it has not been built yet.

## See also

- [Panels](panels.md#the-rule-that-governs-every-attribute) — the per-attribute rule at
  the Python layer, before the UI layer is added on top
- [Lists](lists.md#the-customisation-rail) — the fullest worked example of this cascade
- [Theming](theming.md#the-settings-screen) — the other UI layer, for branding and
  behaviour
- [Settings](settings.md#where-a-value-comes-from) — the `VANTAGE` dict's own cascade
  underneath a `SiteConfiguration` row, the same shape one level up

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/panels/

# Panels

[← Index](index.md)

A `ModelPanel` is one model's configuration: what it is called, which columns its list
page shows, how it can be filtered, what its form looks like, and what may be done to
it. It is ordinary Python, and it lives in a `panel.py` next to your `models.py`.

```python
# blog/panel.py
from vantage import ModelPanel, register

from blog.models import Post


@register(Post)
class PostPanel(ModelPanel):
    list_display = ["title", "author", "status", "published_at"]
```

## The rule that governs every attribute

> **Every attribute defaults to `None`, meaning *infer it*. Setting one attribute
> overrides that attribute and nothing else.**

Configuring `list_display` must never switch off inference for filters, search or
widgets. That is the package's most important ergonomic guarantee, and it is why
inference is resolved per attribute rather than as a single all-or-nothing fallback.

You can see it in the panel class itself: every getter falls back independently.

```python
def get_list_filter(self, request=None) -> list[str]:
    stored = listprefs.override(self, request, "list_filter")   # a UI preference
    if stored is not None:
        return list(stored)
    if self.list_filter is not None:                            # your panel.py
        return list(self.list_filter)
    return inference.infer_list_filter(self.model)              # inference
```

That first branch is not incidental: it is the same **UI override → `panel.py` →
inference** order every configurable surface in the package follows. See
[How configuration resolves](configuration.md) for the one page that states it and
explains why the order runs that way round.

The consequence in practice, from the demo project:

```python
@register(Product)
class ProductPanel(ModelPanel):
    label_plural = "Catalogue"
    icon = "box"
    group = "Commerce"
    list_display = ["name", "sku", "category", "status", "price", "stock"]
```

`ProductPanel` declares columns and nothing else. Asking the live panel what it
resolves confirms the rest is still inferred:

```pycon
>>> panel = site.get_panel(Product)
>>> panel.get_list_display()
['name', 'sku', 'category', 'status', 'price', 'stock']     # yours
>>> panel.get_list_filter()
['status', 'is_featured', 'created_at', 'category']         # inferred
>>> panel.get_list_search()
['sku', 'name', 'description', 'category__name']            # inferred
```

## Registering

Three ways, all equivalent.

```python
from vantage import ModelPanel, register, site

# 1. The decorator — the usual one.
@register(Post)
class PostPanel(ModelPanel):
    ...

# 2. Explicitly, against the default site.
site.register(Post, PostPanel)

# 3. With no panel at all, taking every default.
site.register(Post)
```

Auto-registration runs *after* `panel.py` discovery and never clobbers an existing
registration, so an explicit panel always wins over inference whichever ran first.
Registering the same model twice raises `AlreadyRegistered`.

`site.unregister(Model)` removes one. It raises `NotRegistered` if the model was not
there.

## Identity

| Attribute | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `str` | `Meta.verbose_name`, capitalised | Singular name in headings and buttons |
| `label_plural` | `str` | `Meta.verbose_name_plural`, capitalised | Plural name in the sidebar, the page title and the export filename |
| `icon` | `str` | guessed from the model name | Sidebar and palette icon |
| `group` | `str` | the app's `verbose_name` | Which sidebar group the model sits in |
| `order` | `int` | `0` | Sorts sidebar groups; lower comes first, and may be negative |
| `description` | `str` | `None` | A sentence under the list-page heading |

```python
@register(Order)
class OrderPanel(ModelPanel):
    label = "Order"
    label_plural = "Orders"
    icon = "shopping-cart"
    group = "Commerce"
    order = -10
    description = "Every order placed in the last six months."
```

Icons are [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) names. When `icon` is unset, a small table of
common model names supplies one for free — `user` → `users`, `order` → `shopping-cart`,
`post` → `file-text`, `category` → `folder` — and anything unlisted falls back to `box`.

`order` sorts *groups*, not items: a group takes the lowest `order` of any panel in it,
and items inside a group are sorted alphabetically. To control item order too, declare
[`NAV`](settings.md#navigation).

## The list page

| Attribute | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_display` | `list[str]` | inferred | Columns, in order. Field paths, model attributes or panel methods |
| `list_link` | `str` | inferred | Which column opens the record |
| `list_filter` | `list[str]` | inferred | Filter rail. Real field paths only — they are resolved in SQL |
| `list_search` | `list[str]` | inferred | Fields the search box covers. Real field paths only |
| `search_fields` | `list[str]` | `None` | Alias for `list_search`, for `contrib.admin` muscle memory |
| `list_editable` | `list[str]` | `None` | Columns editable in place on the list page |
| `list_per_page` | `int` | `DEFAULT_PER_PAGE` (50) | Rows per page |
| `ordering` | `list[str]` | inferred | Default sort. `Meta.ordering` wins if you set neither |

`list_display` entries may traverse relations with `__`, and may also name a method on
the panel or an attribute on the model:

```python
@register(Order)
class OrderPanel(ModelPanel):
    list_display = ["number", "customer__name", "status", "total", "line_count"]

    def line_count(self, obj):
        return obj.items.count()
```

`list_filter` and `list_search` are stricter: their entries are fed straight to the ORM,
so a panel method is not acceptable there and `manage.py check` says so
(`vantage.E011` / `vantage.E012`).

`list_search` reaches one hop into a foreign key. Searching an order by its customer's
name is what a human means by "search", and it is the single most common thing people
add by hand to a Django admin — so inference does it for you.

Details: [Lists](lists.md).

## List views

| Attribute | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_views` | `list[str]` | inferred | Views the switcher offers, first is the default. `["table"]` switches the others off |
| `kanban_field` | `str` | inferred | Choices or boolean field the board has one column per value of |
| `calendar_field` | `str` | inferred | Date or datetime field the calendar places records by |
| `kanban_fields` | `list[str]` | inferred | What the board's "Group by" picker offers; `[]` hides it |
| `calendar_fields` | `list[str]` | inferred | What the calendar's "Dates from" picker offers; `[]` hides it |
| `gallery_field` | `str` | inferred | Image (or picture-named file) field a gallery card leads with |
| `map_fields` | `str` or `(str, str)` | inferred | A `PointField`, or a `("latitude", "longitude")` pair |
| `card_fields` | `list[str]` | inferred | Fields under a card's title on the board and in the gallery |

Details: [List views](list-views.md).

## List analytics

| Attribute | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_stats` | `list[Stat]` | `None` | Number cards above the table, computed over the filtered queryset |
| `list_charts` | `list[Chart]` | `None` | Charts above the table, drawn as server-side SVG |
| `list_aggregates` | `dict[str, str \| type]` | `None` | Overrides the per-column footer aggregate |

```python
from django.db.models import Avg, Count, Q, Sum
from vantage import Chart, ModelPanel, Stat, register


@register(Order)
class OrderPanel(ModelPanel):
    list_stats = [
        Stat("Revenue", Sum("total"), format="currency", trend="created_at"),
        Stat("Orders", Count("id")),
        Stat("Average order", Avg("total"), format="currency"),
        Stat("Refunded", Count("id", filter=Q(status="refunded")), tone="destructive"),
    ]
    list_charts = [
        Chart.timeseries("Revenue over time", date="created_at", value=Sum("total")),
        Chart.breakdown("By status", group_by="status", value=Count("id"), kind="donut"),
    ]
    list_aggregates = {"total": "sum", "stock": None}
```

`list_aggregates` accepts a function name (`"sum"`, `"avg"`, `"min"`, `"max"`,
`"count"`), an aggregate class (`Sum`) so it reads naturally next to the `Stat`
declarations above it, or `None` to suppress a column the footer would otherwise sum.

The summary bar needs no configuration at all: a money column is summed, a rating
column is averaged, and an identifier is left alone. Details:
[Analytics](analytics.md).

## The detail and form pages

| Attribute | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | `list[str]` | inferred | Which fields the form contains, in order |
| `exclude` | `list[str]` | `None` | Names removed from whatever `fields` or inference produced |
| `layout` | `Node` | `None` | Tabs, sections and rows — see the [layout DSL](forms.md#the-layout-dsl) |
| `readonly_fields` | `list[str]` | `None` | Shown but not editable, and *removed from the form entirely* |
| `inlines` | `list[type[Inline]]` | `None` | Child records editable on the parent's own form — see [Editable inlines](forms.md#editable-inlines) |
| `related_tabs` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Group the detail page's related-record blocks into a tab strip. `None` decides by count (two or more); `True`/`False` assert it either way — see [The record page](forms.md#the-record-page) |
| `sensitive_fields` | `list[str]` | inferred | Fields masked on every surface, revealable one at a time. A list replaces inference; `[]` switches masking off — see [Sensitive fields](sensitive-fields.md) |
| `field_permissions` | `dict[str, dict[str, str]]` | `None` | Per role, fields that are `"hidden"` or `"readonly"`: `{"Support": {"price": "readonly"}}`. Added to the rules the roles matrix stores — see [Field permissions](field-permissions.md) |
| `read_only` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Refuse add, delete and field changes for everyone; `None` follows `UNMANAGED_READ_ONLY` for unmanaged models — see [Read-only models](permissions.md#read-only-models-and-legacy-databases) |
| `editable_fields` | `list[str]` | `None` | With `read_only`, the fields that stay changeable on existing rows |
| `formfield_overrides` | `dict[type[Field], dict]` | `None` | Form-field arguments per model field class, with `django.contrib.admin`'s semantics: `{models.TextField: {"widget": MyEditor}}` — see [Overriding a widget](forms.md#overriding-a-widget) |
| `widgets` | `dict[str, Widget]` | `None` | A widget per field name, winning over `formfield_overrides`: `{"body": MyEditor}` |

`readonly_fields` is a security boundary rather than a UI affordance. A readonly field
is not rendered as a control **and** is not in the form's field list, so a hand-crafted
POST that includes it is dropped by `construct_instance` rather than merely unrendered.

A name in `readonly_fields` that inference did not pick up is appended rather than
dropped — the canonical case being `readonly_fields = ["created_at"]` on an
`auto_now_add` column, which is not an editable field at all and would otherwise vanish
from a page whose whole purpose was to display it.

`inlines` is unset by default — nothing is inferred here, because guessing which of a
model's reverse relations belong on the parent's own form (rather than as the
read-only [related blocks](forms.md#the-record-page) the detail page already shows)
is a judgement call the package should not make for you. Full treatment, including a
gotcha worth knowing before you rely on the default: [Forms](forms.md#editable-inlines).

Details: [Forms](forms.md).

## Behaviour

| Attribute | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions` | `list[str \| Action]` | `None` | Bulk actions offered on the list page |
| `row_actions` | `list[str]` | `None` | Which actions appear in the menu on each list row — see below |
| `undo` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Whether deletes and edits offer **Undo** in their toast. `None` follows `UNDO_WINDOW`; `False` turns it off for this model — see [Undo](undo.md) |
| `history` | `bool \| "view" \| None` | `None` | The record's [History](history.md) page and restoring from it. `None` follows `AUDIT_LOG`; `"view"` keeps the page without restore; `False` removes it |
| `requires_approval` | `list[str]` | `None` | Fields whose changes wait for someone with `<app>.approve_<model>` before they are saved; the rest of an edit saves as usual — see [Approvals](approvals.md) |
| `checks_class` | `type` | `ModelPanelChecks` | Subclass it to extend validation for your own panel base class |

When `actions` is left unset, every method on the panel decorated with `@action` is
discovered. Decorating a method is already an explicit statement of intent, so
requiring it to be listed a second time would be ceremony:

```python
from vantage import ModelPanel, action, register


@register(Review)
class ReviewPanel(ModelPanel):
    @action("Publish", icon="check", permission="change")
    def publish(self, request, queryset):
        return f"Published {queryset.update(is_published=True)} reviews."

    @action("Delete", icon="trash", permission="delete", destructive=True,
            max_rows=500, confirm="Permanently delete {count} reviews?")
    def delete_selected(self, request, queryset):
        deleted, _ = queryset.delete()
        return f"Deleted {deleted} records."
```

Set `actions = []` to offer none, or list names to choose a subset and their order.
Details: [Bulk actions](lists.md#bulk-actions).

### Row actions

Bulk actions apply to a selection; `row_actions` puts the same kind of thing — plus a
handful of built-ins — into a menu on **one row**, so a reviewer never has to select a
single record just to publish it.

```python
@register(Review)
class ReviewPanel(ModelPanel):
    row_actions = ["view", "edit", "duplicate", "publish", "delete"]

    @action("Publish", icon="check")
    def publish(self, request, queryset):
        return f"Published {queryset.update(is_published=True)} reviews."
```

`row_actions` is not a second decorator or a second way of declaring behaviour — it is
a list of names, and each name resolves to one of two things:

- **A built-in**: `"view"`/`"detail"`, `"edit"`/`"change"`, `"duplicate"`/`"copy"`, or
  `"delete"`. Each renders as an ordinary link to the page that already does the job —
  see [Duplicating a record](forms.md#duplicating-a-record) for exactly what the
  duplicate page does with unique fields, files and related children.
- **The name of an `@action`-decorated method** — the exact same decorator [bulk
  actions](lists.md#bulk-actions) use, read for its label, icon, permission and
  `confirm` text rather than restated. It renders as a `POST` button, never a link, so
  a crawler cannot fire it.

Leaving `row_actions` unset offers nothing beyond what the row already links to. A
soft-deleted row gets a Restore button automatically wherever the [`soft_delete`
pattern](#detected-conventions) applies — that one is not declarable in `row_actions`
at all, because it only makes sense on a trashed row and never on a live one. See
[Deleting, and undoing it](lists.md#deleting-and-undoing-it) for what Delete and
Restore actually do to the row, and why a second Delete on an already-trashed row
destroys it for good.

For content that is not an action at all — a badge, a status dot, a link to somewhere
outside the panel — use the `row_actions` [slot](extending.md#slots) instead, which is
a different mechanism with the same name: it contributes arbitrary HTML to the same
trailing cell rather than declaring a button with a permission and a confirmation. A
panel that overrides `slot()` without calling `super()` loses its declared
`row_actions` silently, because rendering them is itself implemented as a slot
contribution — worth knowing if you use both on the same panel.

## Overridable methods

Where an attribute cannot express what you need, override the method behind it. Each
one takes `request`, so the answer can depend on who is asking.

| Method | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `get_queryset(request)` | `QuerySet` | The base queryset for **every** view. Override to scope rows per tenant |
| `get_list_queryset(request)` | `QuerySet` | The list page's queryset, with `select_related`/`prefetch_related` already planned |
| `get_list_display(request)` | `list[str]` | |
| `get_list_link(request)` | `str` | |
| `get_list_filter(request)` | `list[str]` | |
| `get_list_search(request)` | `list[str]` | |
| `get_ordering(request)` | `list[str]` | |
| `get_per_page(request)` | `int` | |
| `get_label()` / `get_label_plural()` | `str` | |
| `get_group()` | `str` | |
| `get_icon()` | `str` | |
| `get_patterns()` | `ModelPatterns` | The [conventions](#detected-conventions) detected on this model |
| `get_trash_queryset(request)` | `QuerySet` | Soft-deleted rows, or an empty queryset |
| `get_sensitive_fields()` | `frozenset[str]` | The masked field names — `sensitive_fields`, or inference |
| `can_reveal(request, obj, field_name)` | `bool` | Whether this request may reveal one value. Default: superusers and `vantage.reveal_sensitive` — see [Revealing a value](sensitive-fields.md#revealing-a-value) |
| `get_requires_approval()` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `requires_approval`, minus any entry a check reports (E106–E108) |

`get_list_queryset` derives its optimisation from what the page actually renders — every
column and every search path — so a column added to `list_display` cannot reintroduce
an N+1. The test suite asserts that with `assertNumQueries`.

`get_trash_queryset` starts from `_base_manager` when the model's default manager
already hides soft-deleted rows. A trash view built on `get_queryset()` would filter a
queryset that can never contain what it is looking for, and silently show nothing.

### Read-only properties

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| `model` | The model class |
| `opts` | `model._meta` |
| `slug` | URL segment: `shop.Order` → `shop-order` |
| `list_url_name` | `vantage:shop-order-list` |
| `count` | `model._default_manager.count()` |

## Permission hooks

Define any of these on the panel and Vantage consults it before its own answer. The
signature is `(request, obj=None)` for all four verbs — including `add`, where
`contrib.admin` omits `obj`. One uniform signature is worth more than
bug-compatibility with an inconsistency, and the
[`contrib.admin` adapter](extending.md) bridges the difference for adopted admins.

```python
@register(Invoice)
class InvoicePanel(ModelPanel):
    def has_delete_permission(self, request, obj=None):
        return False        # nobody deletes an invoice, ever
```

`has_view_permission`, `has_add_permission`, `has_change_permission` and
`has_delete_permission` are consulted **before the superuser bypass**, deliberately. A
panel that says nobody may delete these rows means nobody.

Returning `None` means "no opinion" and hands the decision back to the normal chain.
Row-level scoping does not belong here — see
[why `filter_queryset` must be bulk](permissions.md#why-filter_queryset-must-be-bulk).

## Save hook

Define `save_model(request, obj, form, change)` and Vantage hands you the populated but
unsaved instance, which is the point: it is where you set what the form cannot.

```python
@register(Article)
class ArticlePanel(ModelPanel):
    readonly_fields = ["author"]

    def save_model(self, request, obj, form, change):
        if not change:
            obj.author = request.user
        obj.save()
```

The hook must call `obj.save()` itself. Vantage writes the many-to-many relations
afterwards, so that is one thing every hook does not have to remember. The same hook is
used by the CSV importer and by inline cell editing, so a rule written once applies to
all three write paths.

## Detected conventions

Vantage recognises the modelling conventions the Django community has settled on, and
offers the matching affordance with no configuration at all: a tree view for a
hierarchy, a trash bin with restore for a soft delete, time grouping for a date column,
publish/unpublish buttons for a publication flag, currency formatting for a money
column.

Seven detectors run, and each is pure: model in, description out. No queries, no
request, no clock. The bar for a detection is deliberately higher than for column
inference, because a false positive costs more than a miss — a model wrongly treated as
soft-deleted *hides rows*. Every detector therefore wants both a name the convention
dictates **and** a field type that makes the convention work.

| Pattern | Recognises | Switch off | Name the field |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree` | a self-FK called `parent`, django-mptt, django-treebeard | `tree = False` | `tree_parent_field = "..."` |
| `soft_delete` | `deleted_at`, `date_deleted`, `deleted_on`, `is_deleted`, `deleted` | `soft_delete = False` | `soft_delete_field = "archived_at"` |
| `timeline` | a date to group rows by, preferring a domain date over an audit stamp | `timeline = False` | `timeline_field = "..."` |
| `sortable` | `position`, `sort_order`, `display_order`, `sequence`, `order`, `sort` | `sortable = False` | `sortable_field = "..."` |
| `publishable` | a `status` choice field, `is_published`, or `published_at` | `publishable = False` | `publishable_field = "..."` |
| `ownership` | `owner`, `user`, `created_by`, `author`, `creator`, `added_by` | `ownership = False` | `owner_field = "..."` |
| `money` | a field name ending in `price`, `total`, `amount`, `cost`, `fee`, `balance`, `revenue` | `money = False` | `money_fields = [...]` |

Setting the boolean to `True` asserts the convention and waives the naming rule — with
one exception: `tree = True` on a model with two self-referential foreign keys still
needs `tree_parent_field`, because which one is the parent would otherwise be a coin
flip.

Inspect what fired:

```pycon
>>> site.get_panel(Customer).get_patterns().detected
('soft_delete', 'timeline')
>>> site.get_panel(Category).get_patterns().detected
('tree',)
>>> site.get_panel(Review).get_patterns().detected
('timeline', 'publishable')
>>> site.get_panel(Order).get_patterns().money
(MoneyField(name='total', decimal_places=2),)
```

A model with a publication flag and no declared actions gets publish and unpublish
actions for free. That happens **only** when the panel offers no actions of its own: an
author who wrote actions has thought about which ones belong, and silently adding two
more to their list is the kind of helpfulness that reads as a bug.

## Validation

`manage.py check` validates every user-written panel. Panels left entirely at their
defaults are skipped.

| ID | Reported when |
|---|---|
| `vantage.E010` | `list_display` names something that is not a field, a model attribute or a panel method |
| `vantage.E011` | `list_filter` names something that is not a real field path |
| `vantage.E012` | `list_search` names something that is not a real field path |
| `vantage.E013` | `ordering` names something that is not a real field path |
| `vantage.E014` | `list_link` is not one of the columns in `list_display` |
| `vantage.E015` | `list_editable` names something that is not a field |
| `vantage.E016` | A column is in both `list_editable` and `list_link` |
| `vantage.E017` | `layout` names a field the model does not have |
| `vantage.E018` | `list_select_related` names something that is not a field path, or crosses a multi-valued relation `select_related` cannot follow |
| `vantage.E019` | `related_tabs` is set to something other than `True`, `False` or `None` |
| `vantage.E020` | A [removed attribute](#removed-attributes) — currently only `permissions` — is still set |
| `vantage.E070` | `list_views` is not a non-empty list, or names a view that does not exist |
| `vantage.E071` | `list_views` names a view the model has no field for |
| `vantage.E072` | `kanban_field` is not a local field with 2–12 choices, or a `BooleanField` |
| `vantage.E073` | `calendar_field` is not a `DateField` or `DateTimeField` |
| `vantage.E074` | `gallery_field` is not an `ImageField` or `FileField` |
| `vantage.E075` | `map_fields` is neither a `PointField` nor a pair of `FloatField`/`DecimalField`s |
| `vantage.E076` | `card_fields` names something that is not a field, a model attribute or a panel method |
| `vantage.E078` | `kanban_fields` is not a list, or names a field a board cannot be grouped by |
| `vantage.E079` | `calendar_fields` is not a list, or names something that is not a date |
| `vantage.E077` | `undo` is set to something other than `True`, `False` or `None` |
| `vantage.E091` | `history` is set to something other than `True`, `False`, `"view"` or `None` |
| `vantage.E092` | `history = True` while `VANTAGE["AUDIT_LOG"]` is off |
| `vantage.E090` | `sensitive_fields` is not a list, or names something that is not a field or attribute |
| `vantage.W090` | `list_search`/`search_fields`, `list_filter` or `ordering` explicitly names a [sensitive field](sensitive-fields.md); it is dropped at request time |
| `vantage.E105` | `requires_approval` is not a list of field names |
| `vantage.E106` | `requires_approval` names something that is not a field of the model |
| `vantage.E107` | `requires_approval` names a field the panel's form does not let anyone edit (not editable, readonly, excluded or left out of `fields`) |
| `vantage.E108` | `requires_approval` names a many-to-many, a reverse relation or a file field, which cannot be held back |
| `vantage.E110` | `field_permissions` is not a dict of role name to rules |
| `vantage.E111` | A `field_permissions` entry does not map a role name to a dict of field name to level |
| `vantage.E112` | `field_permissions` names something that is not a field of the model |
| `vantage.E113` | `field_permissions` sets a level other than `"hidden"` or `"readonly"` |
| `vantage.E114` | `field_permissions` restricts the primary key |
| `vantage.E122` | `read_only` is not `True`, `False` or `None` |
| `vantage.E123` | `editable_fields` is not a list, or names something that is not an editable field |
| `vantage.E124` | `agent_access` is not `"none"`, `"read"`, `"write"` or `None` |
| `vantage.E125` | `agent_hidden_fields` is not a list of field names, or names something that is not a field |
| `vantage.E120` | `formfield_overrides` is not a dict of model field class to a dict of form field arguments |
| `vantage.E121` | `widgets` is not a dict, names something that is not a field, or maps one to something that is not a form widget |

`vantage.E020` is also issued from an unrelated place, `nav.py`, for a malformed
[`NAV`](settings.md#navigation) entry — the same numeric id covers two different
mistakes, which is a quirk of the current numbering rather than a hint that the two are
connected; read the message, not the id, if you hit it.

To extend this for your own panel base class, subclass `ModelPanelChecks` and point
`checks_class` at it.

## Declared but not yet wired up

Nothing, currently. `inlines`, `row_actions`, `list_select_related`, `related_tabs` and
`layout` all used to belong on this list and no longer do:

- [Editable inlines](forms.md#editable-inlines) and [Row actions](#row-actions) above.
- `list_select_related` **is** read: it is unioned into the query plan the optimiser
  already derives from the rendered columns (`get_list_queryset`), and it is validated
  (`vantage.E018`) — set it only for a join the optimiser has no other reason to make,
  such as one your own overridden `get_list_queryset` needs but no column or search
  path names.
- `related_tabs` groups the detail page's related-record blocks into a tab strip once
  there is a choice to make — two or more blocks by default, or always/never with an
  explicit `True`/`False`. See [The record page](forms.md#the-record-page).
- `layout` — `Tabs`, `Tab`, `Section` and `Row` — now replaces the fixed-section
  grouping on the create/edit form outright. See [The layout DSL](forms.md#the-layout-dsl).

## Removed attributes

`ModelPanel.permissions` does not exist. It is not silently ignored — setting it fails
`manage.py check` outright, as `vantage.E020`:

```
ERRORS:
<class 'InvoicePanel'>: (vantage.E020) 'permissions' is no longer a Vantage panel
attribute.
    HINT: Access is resolved in one place. Define has_view_permission /
    has_add_permission / has_change_permission / has_delete_permission on the panel,
    or point VANTAGE['PERMISSIONS'] at a PanelPermissions subclass.
```

A second declarative mechanism for the same decision is how two answers to "may this
user delete?" end up disagreeing, so it was removed rather than left dormant. Use the
[per-panel hooks](#permission-hooks) or [`VANTAGE["PERMISSIONS"]`](permissions.md#swapping-the-resolver)
instead.

## Second panels and second sites

A proxy model is the normal way to give one table two differently-configured presences
in the panel. Proxy models are deliberately kept by auto-registration for that reason.

```python
class UnpaidOrder(Order):
    class Meta:
        proxy = True
        verbose_name = "unpaid order"


@register(UnpaidOrder)
class UnpaidOrderPanel(ModelPanel):
    group = "Commerce"

    def get_queryset(self, request):
        return super().get_queryset(request).filter(status="pending")
```

For a genuinely separate panel — a staff panel and a partner panel, say — instantiate
`VantageSite` again and mount it at another URL:

```python
from vantage import VantageSite

partner_site = VantageSite(name="partner")
partner_site.register(Order, PartnerOrderPanel)

urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", site.urls),
    path("partner/", partner_site.urls),
]
```

Note that the `VANTAGE` settings dict is global: both sites share the branding, the
navigation declaration and the permission resolver.

## See also

- [How configuration resolves](configuration.md) — the UI-override layer that sits in
  front of every getter this page describes
- [Inference](inference.md) — what the defaults will be
- [Lists](lists.md) — the list page in detail
- [Forms](forms.md) — widgets, layout, readonly, delete preview, editable inlines
- [Permissions](permissions.md) — the three-layer model
