```bash
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=tests.settings PYTHONPATH=/path/to/django-vantage \
  django-admin makemessages -l fr
```

Translate the strings that matter for a working panel — you do not have to fill in
all ~1,700 entries before a locale is useful. Leave the rest with an empty `msgstr`;
that falls back to English rather than shipping a guess. Re-run `compilemessages`
after every edit; the `.po` is not read at runtime, only the compiled `.mo` is.

## JavaScript strings

The runtime under `src/vantage/static/vantage/*.js` — the combobox, the inline grid
editor, the upload widget, the palette — has plenty of user-facing text: the
combobox's "N results shown" and "No matches for…", the inline editor's "N changes"
and "Discard N unsaved changes?". All of it goes through
[Django's JavaScript catalogue](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/stable/topics/i18n/translation/#internationalization-in-javascript-code),
so the panel does not fall back to English the moment it starts speaking to you
interactively.

The catalogue is mounted at `_/jsi18n/` with `packages=["vantage"]`, which scopes it
to this package's own strings — a project's translations are its own view to add, and
serving them from here would make one catalogue responsible for two things. It is
cached for a day: the response is identical for everyone in a given language, and
generating it walks every `.mo` file's plural forms. Django keys that cache by the
active language automatically when `USE_I18N` is on, so there is no Vary header to
get wrong.

`base.html` loads the catalogue and then `vantage-i18n-fallback.js`, in that order and
neither deferred. The fallback defines `gettext`, `ngettext`, `interpolate`,
`pgettext`, `npgettext` and `gettext_noop` as pass-throughs **only if the catalogue
did not already define them** — so a project that has not run `collectstatic`, or
whose proxy has eaten the route, gets English rather than a `gettext is not defined`
that stops every script on the page.

Plurals go through `ngettext`, and interpolation through `interpolate` with whole
sentences: `gettext("Showing %s of %s")`, never a translated fragment concatenated to
a number, because word order is not universal. Arabic is the useful test here — it has
six plural forms, and the inline editor's change counter is translated across all of
them.

Deliberately left untranslated: single-glyph button labels (B, I, •, ↑, ↓), keyboard
key names ("Ctrl+B"), and byte-unit abbreviations (B/KB/MB), matching how the Python
side treats the same cases.

To extract them after a change:

```bash
cd src/vantage
django-admin makemessages -d djangojs -l ar
django-admin compilemessages
```

## Testing

`tests/test_i18n.py` renders real pages under
`django.utils.translation.override("ar")` and asserts on the actual response body —
`dir="rtl"` on `<html>`, a known string coming back in Arabic, an untranslated string
falling back to English rather than going blank — plus every one of Arabic's six
`ngettext` plural categories (zero, one, two, few, many, other), and that a built
wheel really contains the compiled `.mo` files. A test that only checks the
catalogue file exists on disk would pass even if the translation pipeline were
completely broken; none of these do.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/extending/

# Extending Vantage

Three extension points, in the order you are likely to need them.

| You want to | Use |
|---|---|
| Put your own HTML on a Vantage page | [Slots](#slots) |
| Ship an extension as an installable package | [Plugins](#plugins) |
| Keep the `admin.py` you already have | [The `contrib.admin` adapter](#the-contribadmin-adapter) |

---

## Slots

A slot is a named place in a Vantage template that you can fill from Python. It exists
so that adding one banner does not mean overriding — and then maintaining — a whole
template.

### The eight slots

| Name | Where |
|---|---|
| `before_list` / `after_list` | above / below the grid on a list page |
| `before_form` / `after_form` | above / below a create or edit form |
| `object_actions` | the button row on a detail page |
| `row_actions` | a trailing cell on every list row |
| `detail_sidebar` | beside the fields on a detail page |
| `dashboard_top` | above the dashboard cards |

### Filling one

Anywhere that runs at startup — `panel.py` is the natural home:

```python
# blog/panel.py
from django.utils.html import format_html

from vantage import slots

# A template fragment.
slots.add("before_list", template="blog/_import_banner.html")

# Or a callable. It receives the template context as a plain dict.
@slots.slot("object_actions")
def preview_button(context):
    post = context["object"]
    return format_html('<a class="v-btn v-btn-ghost" href="{}">Preview</a>', post.get_absolute_url())
```

Contributions render in registration order. Pass `order=-10` to sit ahead of everything
registered by someone else — that is how a plugin gets in front of project code without
either importing the other.

### Escaping

A callable's return value is escaped unless you marked it safe:

```python
slots.add("before_list", render=lambda ctx: "<b>hi</b>")            # renders &lt;b&gt;hi&lt;/b&gt;
slots.add("before_list", render=lambda ctx: format_html("<b>hi</b>"))  # renders <b>hi</b>
```

A `template=` contribution is not escaped again — the template engine already escaped
its own variables on the way through.

### Permissions

```python
slots.add("row_actions", template="blog/_retry.html", permission="blog.change_post")
slots.add("dashboard_top", render=beta_banner, permission=lambda request: request.user.is_staff)
```

A string goes to `request.user.has_perm`; a callable receives the request. A gated
contribution renders nothing when there is no request in context — it fails closed.

### Scoping to one model

```python
slots.add("before_list", template="blog/_post_help.html", model=Post)
```

Or, for content that belongs with the panel, implement the hook instead:

```python
@register(Post)
class PostPanel(ModelPanel):
    def slot(self, name, context):
        if name == "detail_sidebar":
            return render_to_string("blog/_seo_card.html", context)
        return None
```

The panel's own content renders first, then the registry's.

### Failure

One contribution raising does not take the page down: the exception is logged to the
`vantage.slots` logger and that fragment is skipped. Its siblings still render.

### Using a slot in your own template

If you override a Vantage template and want a slot of your own:

```python
slots.declare("my_sidebar")
```

```django
{% load vantage_slots %}
{% slot "my_sidebar" %}

{# For markup that should only exist when the slot has content: #}
{% slot_filled "row_actions" as has_actions %}
{% if has_actions %}<td>{% slot "row_actions" object=row.obj %}</td>{% endif %}
```

Undeclared names are rejected at registration, because a mistyped slot name is
otherwise invisible — the fragment simply never appears.

---

## Plugins

A plugin is a package that extends the panel by being installed.

### Writing one

```python
# vantage_celery/__init__.py
from vantage import slots
from vantage.plugins import VantagePlugin
from vantage_celery.pages import QueuePage


class CeleryPlugin(VantagePlugin):
    name = "celery"
    version = "1.2.0"

    def register(self, site):
        site.register_page(QueuePage)
        slots.add("dashboard_top", template="vantage_celery/_queue_depth.html")
```

```toml
# vantage_celery/pyproject.toml
[project.entry-points."vantage.plugins"]
celery = "vantage_celery:CeleryPlugin"
```

`pip install vantage-celery` is now the whole installation. No settings change, no
`INSTALLED_APPS` entry.

`register(site)` runs inside `AppConfig.ready()`, so it must not touch the database — a
query there breaks `migrate` on a fresh install.

An entry point may also point at an instance, or at a bare function taking the site:

```python
def setup(site):
    site.register_page(QueuePage)
```

### Registering one by hand

For a plugin you vendor, or if you would rather see your extensions written down:

```python
# project/panel.py
from vantage.plugins import register_plugin
from vantage_celery import CeleryPlugin

register_plugin(CeleryPlugin)
```

This loads immediately, and is a no-op if the same plugin was already discovered — so
doing both is harmless.

### Turning one off

```python
VANTAGE = {
    "PLUGINS": ["celery", "audit"],   # allowlist; None (the default) loads everything
    "PLUGINS_EXCLUDE": ["celery"],    # denylist, and it wins
}
```

Names match either the entry-point name or the plugin's own `name`. An excluded plugin
is never imported, which is what makes the denylist useful when the reason for
switching it off is that importing it fails.

### When a plugin is broken

Nothing is fatal. A plugin that fails to import, or whose `register` hook raises, is
skipped and reported by `manage.py check`:

```
WARNINGS:
?: (vantage.E030) The Vantage plugin 'celery' failed to load and was skipped.
    HINT: ImportError: No module named 'kombu'
    Declared at vantage_celery:CeleryPlugin.
    Fix the plugin, or add 'celery' to VANTAGE['PLUGINS_EXCLUDE'] to run without it.
```

The alternative — raising in `ready()` — means no shell, no `migrate`, and no way to
uninstall the thing that broke.

Loading is idempotent, so a second `ready()` (the autoreloader, a test that reconfigures
settings) does not give you two copies of every page.

---

## The `contrib.admin` adapter

Import an existing `ModelAdmin` and get a working panel. Your `admin.py` does not
change, and both panels keep working side by side.

### Everything at once

```python
# project/panel.py
from vantage import site
from vantage.contrib.django_admin import adopt_admin_site

adopt_admin_site(site)
```

Every model registered with `django.contrib.admin` now has a Vantage panel. Models you
have already given a hand-written `ModelPanel` are left alone; pass `replace=True` if
you want the admin to win instead.

Call it from `panel.py` so it runs before auto-registration.

### One model at a time

```python
from vantage import ModelPanel, register
from vantage.contrib.django_admin import from_admin
from blog.admin import PostAdmin
from blog.models import Post


@register(Post)
@from_admin(PostAdmin)
class PostPanel(ModelPanel):
    icon = "file-text"        # anything you declare here wins
    list_per_page = 100
```

If `PostAdmin` is not registered with `contrib.admin`, name the model:
`@from_admin(PostAdmin, Post)`.

### What translates

| `ModelAdmin` | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `list_display` | `list_display` — including methods on the admin, and `__str__` |
| `list_display_links` | `list_link` (the first entry) |
| `list_filter` | `list_filter` (field entries) |
| `search_fields` | `list_search` |
| `ordering`, `list_per_page` | `ordering`, `list_per_page` |
| `list_select_related` | `list_select_related` (`True` gives way to Vantage's own planner) |
| `list_editable` | `list_editable` |
| `fields`, `exclude`, `readonly_fields` | the same, with `fields` flattened |
| `fieldsets` | a `Section` / `Row` layout, `classes=("collapse",)` included |
| `date_hierarchy` | a date filter on that field |
| `actions` | Vantage actions, with `short_description` and `permissions` |
| `has_view/add/change/delete_permission` | the same methods on the panel |
| `get_queryset`, `save_model` | delegated to the admin — the signatures match |
| `get_readonly_fields`, `get_exclude`, `get_fields` | per-request **read-only** field rules through the panel's `get_field_access(request)`, asked with `obj=None` |

Only what the admin actually *declared* is translated. An attribute left at its
`ModelAdmin` default stays unset on the panel, so Vantage's inference still runs:
adopting an admin that sets only `search_fields` does not cost you inferred columns,
filters and widgets.

`has_*_permission` is consulted *before* the superuser bypass, matching
`contrib.admin`: an admin that denies deletion denies it to everyone.

### What does not translate

Nothing is dropped silently. Each of these is reported per model by `manage.py check`
as `vantage.W040`:

- **`inlines`** — not translated automatically; `ModelAdmin.InlineModelAdmin` classes
  do not carry across. Vantage has its own, differently-shaped mechanism —
  [`ModelPanel.inlines`](forms.md#editable-inlines) — but it is declared by hand on the
  new panel rather than inferred from the adopted `ModelAdmin`.
- **`formfield_overrides`** — now translated onto `ModelPanel.formfield_overrides` and no longer reported.
- **`raw_id_fields`, `autocomplete_fields`, `filter_horizontal`, `filter_vertical`,
  `radio_fields`, `prepopulated_fields`** — widget choices; Vantage picks its own.
- **`get_urls()`** — register a `Page` on the Vantage site instead.
- **`Media`** — use `VANTAGE["CUSTOM_CSS"]`.
- **`form`** and the custom templates (`change_form_template` and friends).
- **The view and form hooks** — `get_form`, `get_fieldsets`, `get_list_display`,
  `get_search_results`, `get_actions`, `changelist_view`, `change_view`, `response_add`,
  `formfield_for_foreignkey`, `lookup_allowed`, and the rest: behaviour that lives in
  Python the adapter cannot read.
- **`SimpleListFilter` and list-filter classes** — the *field* stays filterable with
  Vantage's own control; the custom class does not come across.
- **`short_description` on a display method** — the column header falls back to the
  method name.
- **Computed `readonly_fields`** — excluded from the form, but not displayed.
- **A custom action permission** (`@admin.action(permissions=["approve"])`) — the action
  falls back to requiring `change`, and says so.
- **Cosmetics** — `save_as`, `save_on_top`, `view_on_site`, `empty_value_display`,
  `list_max_show_all`, `show_full_result_count`, `actions_on_top`/`_bottom`, `paginator`,
  `sortable_by`.

```
WARNINGS:
<class 'PostAdminPanel'>: (vantage.W040) PostAdmin was adopted for blog.Post, but
4 setting(s) could not be translated.
    HINT: Not carried across:
      · inlines (inline formsets — edit the related model from its own page, …)
      · raw_id_fields (raw id inputs — Vantage uses a searching select for relations)
      · get_urls() (extra URLs hung off the admin — register a Page on the Vantage site)
      · Media (extra CSS/JS — add it with VANTAGE['CUSTOM_CSS'])
```

### `contrib.admin` is optional

Nothing in the core imports it. `adopt_admin_site()` with no arguments soft-detects with
`apps.is_installed("django.contrib.admin")` and does nothing — loudly, in the log — when
it is absent. Passing an `AdminSite` explicitly skips the detection, which is what you
want for a custom admin site:

```python
from myproject.admin import staff_site

adopt_admin_site(site, admin_site=staff_site)
```

---

## Settings reference

```python
VANTAGE = {
    "PLUGINS": None,          # None = load every discovered plugin; a list = allowlist
    "PLUGINS_EXCLUDE": [],    # never loaded, whatever PLUGINS says
}
```

## Check IDs

| ID | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `vantage.E030` | A plugin failed to load and was skipped |
| `vantage.W030` | `VANTAGE["PLUGINS"]` names a plugin nothing provides |
| `vantage.W040` | A `ModelAdmin` was adopted with settings that could not be translated |
| `vantage.E041` | An adopted `ModelAdmin` restricts access with a hook the adapter cannot translate (`formfield_for_foreignkey`, `formfield_for_manytomany`, `formfield_for_choice_field`, `get_form`, `has_module_permission`). Restrict the same thing on the panel, then add the ID to `SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS` |

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/migrating-from-django-admin/

# Migrating from django.contrib.admin

[← Index](index.md)

A project with a hundred models and years of `admin.py` should not switch in one
deploy. The path below keeps both panels running, moves one batch of models at a time,
and leaves the old admin in place until you choose to remove it. Nothing here edits
your `admin.py`.

## 1. Run both side by side

Install Vantage and mount it on a different URL prefix from the admin. Both read the
same database, the same users and the same permissions.

```python
# urls.py
urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", admin.site.urls),        # the panel you have today
    path("panel/", vantage_site.urls),      # Vantage, alongside it
]
```

Add `"vantage"` to `INSTALLED_APPS`, run `python manage.py migrate` (Vantage keeps its
own few tables) and sign in at `/panel/`. At this point every model that is not yet
registered with Vantage is absent from it. That is expected.

## 2. Read the report

```bash
python manage.py vantage_adopt
```

Every `ModelAdmin` registered on `django.contrib.admin.site` is translated in memory
and reported, per model and per attribute, as one of:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `translated` | Carried across, or covered by something Vantage does by default (the line says which). |
| `needs panel code` | Vantage can do it, but it is Python (a column method, an action, a queryset hook) that has to be ported by hand. |
| `unsupported` | Nothing in Vantage does this today. The line gives the reason and the nearest alternative when there is one. |

Useful options:

```bash
python manage.py vantage_adopt --app orders          # one app at a time
python manage.py vantage_adopt --format json > report.json
python manage.py vantage_adopt --admin-site myproject.admin.custom_site
python manage.py vantage_adopt --strict              # exit status 1 if anything is unsupported
```

`--strict` is meant for CI once you have decided what is acceptable: run it on the apps
you have already migrated so a new unsupported setting cannot slip in unnoticed.

Read the `unsupported` rows first. They are the decisions: drop the feature, replace it
with the Vantage equivalent shown, or keep that model in the old admin for now.

## 3. Translate in batches

Pick a batch of models, ideally a whole app that few people depend on to begin with.

**Option A: adopt at runtime.** Fastest way to see the result:

```python
# panel.py
from vantage import site
from vantage.contrib.django_admin import adopt_admin_site

adopt_admin_site(site)
```

Every registered `ModelAdmin` gets a panel, and `manage.py check` lists what could not
be translated (`vantage.W040`). A panel you have already written by hand wins over the
adopted one. See [Extending](extending.md).

**Option B: write the panels out.** Recommended for the long run, because the file is
yours and no longer reads `admin.py`:

```bash
python manage.py vantage_adopt --app orders --write
```

This writes a starter `panel.py` into the app (or into `<dir>/<app>/panel.py` with
`--output-dir`). It never overwrites an existing file unless you pass `--force`. Apps
that are installed packages are skipped unless you give `--output-dir`. Generated files
contain only attributes the adapter translates; everything it could not carry is a
`TODO(vantage_adopt)` comment at the end of the class, for example:

```python
@register(Order)
class OrderPanel(ModelPanel):
    list_display = ["number", "status"]
    list_search = ["number"]
    # TODO(vantage_adopt) action mark_shipped: port it with @action(...)
```

Work through the TODO comments, then delete them. Run `python manage.py check` after
each batch.

## 4. Permissions carry over

Vantage uses Django's own permission system: the same `auth.Permission` rows, groups and
`has_perm` calls the admin uses, so a person who could change orders in the admin can
change them in Vantage and nobody else can. `has_*_permission` methods on a
`ModelAdmin` are translated to the same hooks on the panel and are consulted before the
superuser bypass, so an admin that refuses deletion to everyone still refuses it. See
[Permissions](permissions.md).

Check these two things per batch:

- A custom permission backend (django-guardian, django-rules) works through
  `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS`. Guardian's row filtering needs one setting; see
  [Permissions](permissions.md#third-party-backends).
- Anything gating on `is_staff` is unchanged, since the panel gates on it too.

## 5. Cut over

When a batch behaves, tell the people who use it. Cut over by changing the URL
prefixes: point `/admin/` at Vantage and move the old admin to a prefix only developers
use, or keep it for the models you have not migrated.

```python
urlpatterns = [
    path("panel/", vantage_site.urls),          # was "admin/"
    path("legacy-admin/", admin.site.urls),
]
```

Bookmarks to `/admin/<app>/<model>/` will break when the prefix changes. If that matters,
add redirects for the models you migrated. Do the cut-over for one batch (or one team)
at a time, not all at once.

## 6. Rollback plan

Because Vantage never modifies `admin.py` or the admin's tables, going back is a URL
change:

1. Put the old admin back on its original prefix.
2. Remove the `vantage` URL include (or leave it mounted on the secondary prefix).

What does not roll back is data written through Vantage. It is ordinary rows in your own
tables, but Vantage also keeps its own records (history, saved views, roles, audit log)
in its own tables, which the old admin does not read. Leave the `vantage` app installed
until you are sure; uninstalling it later is a separate migration step. Pin the version
(`django-vantage==<version>`) while migrating, because the API may still change before
1.0.

## Checklist per batch

- [ ] `vantage_adopt --app <label>` reviewed; unsupported items decided.
- [ ] `panel.py` written or adopted; TODO comments resolved.
- [ ] `manage.py check` clean for the app.
- [ ] Each action, filter and permission rule tried by someone who uses it.
- [ ] Third-party admin plugins checked against [Plugin compatibility](plugin-compatibility.md).
- [ ] Cut over (or deferred) and the rollback prefix confirmed to work.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/plugin-compatibility/

# Plugin compatibility

[← Index](index.md)

`django.contrib.admin` has a large ecosystem of packages that subclass `ModelAdmin`,
inject templates or register widgets. Vantage does not run `ModelAdmin` code, so a
package that works by being the base class of an admin does not carry over by itself.
This page says what to do for the common ones. `python manage.py vantage_adopt` flags
the ones it recognises by name.

Status values:

- **Works as-is**: it does not depend on the admin, so it works in your project and
  with Vantage.
- **Vantage equivalent**: Vantage has its own feature that covers the same job.
- **Not supported**: no equivalent today.

| Package | Status | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| django-import-export | Vantage equivalent | List export (CSV, TSV, JSON) and a mapping/preview import wizard are built in: [Export](lists.md#export), [Import](lists.md#import). Resource classes with custom `before_import_row`/`dehydrate_*` logic are not read; port that logic or do the cleanup in the model. `ImportExportModelAdmin` is mapped by `vantage_adopt`. |
| django-simple-history | Vantage equivalent | Every change made through the panel is recorded with a diff and can be restored: [History](history.md). Changes made outside the panel are not seen. Existing `HistoricalXxx` tables stay in your database and stay readable, but Vantage does not import them into its own history. |
| django-reversion | Vantage equivalent (partial) | [History](history.md) and [Undo](undo.md) cover change history and reverting. Reversion's "recover deleted" view and its `VersionAdmin` mixin have no direct counterpart. Reversion itself keeps working in your code. |
| django-filter (admin integration) | Vantage equivalent | Filters are inferred from the model and configured with `list_filter` ([Lists](lists.md#filtering)). A custom `FilterSet` is not read. django-filter used in your own API or views is unaffected. |
| django-ckeditor, django-tinymce | Vantage equivalent (basic editor) | Fields using these open in Vantage's own editor: bold, italic, lists, links, headings, quotes and code ([Rich-text fields](rich-text.md)), with the HTML sanitised on save and on render. The package's own widget, toolbar plugins and uploads are not loaded. Content stays HTML, but only allowlisted tags survive the next save: images, tables and iframes are removed unless you widen the allowlist with `RICHTEXT_EXTRA_TAGS` first. |
| django-object-actions | Vantage equivalent | Bulk actions use `@action` on the panel ([Lists](lists.md#bulk-actions)); buttons on a detail page go in the `object_actions` slot ([Extending](extending.md)). Port the action bodies by hand. |
| django-admin-sortable2 | Not supported | No drag-to-reorder. Sort by the order column; edit it inline with `list_editable`. |
| django-mptt, django-treebeard | Works as-is (display) | Models detected as trees render parent before child, with indentation ([Lists](lists.md#grouping-trees-and-trash)). Drag-to-move in `DraggableMPTTAdmin` has no equivalent. |
| django-guardian | Works as-is | Object permissions are consulted through `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS`. For row filtering, set `VANTAGE["PERMISSIONS"] = "vantage.permissions.GuardianPermissions"`: [Permissions](permissions.md#django-guardian). The `GuardedModelAdmin` object-permission pages are not reproduced. |
| django-rules | Works as-is | Add the backend; predicates apply at the model and object level. Row scoping needs your own `filter_queryset`: [Permissions](permissions.md#django-rules). |
| django-otp, django-two-factor-auth | Vantage equivalent | Built-in TOTP sign-in with recovery codes: [Two-factor sign-in](two-factor.md). These packages protect their own login view; Vantage's second step is separate, and the two are not linked. Do not run both on the same login. Hardware keys and SMS codes are not supported. |
| django-allauth | Works as-is | Allauth owns your user-facing sign-in. Set `LOGIN_URL` to it if you want people to sign in there, or use Vantage's login pages ([Getting started](getting-started.md#signing-in)). Allauth's admin classes for email addresses and social accounts are not translated; register panels for those models if you need to see them. |
| django-unfold, django-jazzmin, other admin themes | Not applicable | These style `django.contrib.admin`. Vantage has its own interface and theme settings ([Theming](theming.md)). Unfold-specific `ModelAdmin` options (sections, conditional fields, custom dashboard callbacks) are not read; see [Comparison](comparison.md). |
| Anything else that subclasses `ModelAdmin` | Not read | `vantage_adopt` reports unknown base classes as "needs panel code". Check what the base class adds (extra views, templates, URLs) and port it as a panel method or a `Page`. |

## How to check your own project

```bash
python manage.py vantage_adopt --format json | jq '.models[].attributes[] | select(.attribute | startswith("mixin"))'
```

Every third-party base class on your admins appears as a `mixin ...` row with its status.

If a package here is marked "Works as-is" but something behaves differently, treat it as
a bug in this page and report it; the table is based on what the code does, not on
testing every version of every package.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/comparison/

# Vantage vs Unfold (and other contrib.admin themes)

[← Index](index.md)

This is a comparison of approach, written from the Vantage side, so read it with that in
mind. It lists what is different and when each is the better choice. It contains no
benchmark numbers: see [Benchmarks](benchmarks.md) for how to measure on your own data.

## The core difference

[Unfold](https://github.com/unfoldadmin/django-unfold) and similar packages (Jazzmin,
Grappelli, django-admin-interface) **restyle and extend `django.contrib.admin`**. Your
`ModelAdmin` classes, `admin.site`, third-party admin mixins and the admin's templates
stay; you gain a new look and extra options.

Vantage **replaces** the admin. Panels are configured with `ModelPanel`, pages are built
from Vantage's own views and templates, and `ModelAdmin` code is not run (the
[adapter](extending.md) translates the common attributes, and `vantage_adopt` reports
the rest).

## Feature comparison

| | Vantage | Unfold / admin themes |
|---|---|---|
| Built on | Its own views and templates | `django.contrib.admin` |
| Existing `admin.py` | Translated, not run; see [Migrating](migrating-from-django-admin.md) | Used unchanged |
| Third-party admin plugins | Not run; equivalents for several ([Plugin compatibility](plugin-compatibility.md)) | Mostly work, since the admin is still there (Unfold ships integrations for some) |
| Columns, filters, search | Inferred from the model; overriding one keeps the rest inferred | Declared in `ModelAdmin`, as in the stock admin |
| Query optimisation | `select_related`/`prefetch_related` derived from the columns shown | As in the stock admin: declare `list_select_related` yourself |
| Dashboard and charts | Built in, declared in Python ([Pages and dashboards](pages-and-dashboards.md), [Analytics](analytics.md)) | Dashboard components are provided; you write the callback |
| List views | Table, plus kanban, calendar, map and gallery when the model fits ([List views](list-views.md)) | Table |
| Saved views, column preferences | Built in, per user and shared | Not part of the base theme |
| Import and export | Built in | Via django-import-export (Unfold has a styled integration) |
| Change history, undo, approvals | Built in ([History](history.md), [Undo](undo.md), [Approvals](approvals.md)) | Via third-party packages, or the stock `LogEntry` |
| Field-level permissions, roles | Built in ([Field permissions](field-permissions.md), [Roles](roles.md)) | Stock Django permissions; plugins for more |
| Two-factor sign-in | Built in (TOTP) | Via django-otp or similar |
| JSON API | Built in, same permission path as the UI ([API](api.md)) | None |
| Inline formsets, nested editing | `ModelPanel.inlines`; hand-declared | Stock inlines, restyled; extra options such as tabbed inlines |
| Rich-text and widget packages | Built-in sanitised WYSIWYG editor ([Rich-text fields](rich-text.md)); third-party widget JavaScript is not loaded | Works with admin widgets |
| Theming | Brand colour, radius, light/dark, presets ([Theming](theming.md)) | Extensive theming and configuration |
| Maturity | Beta; provisional parts of the API may change before 1.0 ([FAQ](faq.md)) | Established project with a larger user base |
| Python / Django | Python 3.12+, Django 5.2 to 6.1 | See that project's documentation |

Entries in the right-hand column describe how the stock admin and typical themes work;
check the Unfold documentation for its current feature set, which changes.

## When to choose which

**Choose a theme such as Unfold when:**

- you rely on third-party admin packages and do not want to replace them;
- you have a large `admin.py` and the goal is a better look, not a different tool;
- you need a stable, widely used dependency today.

**Choose Vantage when:**

- you want columns, filters, search and query optimisation inferred, with little
  configuration per model;
- you want history, undo, approvals, roles, saved views, import/export and a JSON API
  without assembling packages;
- you are starting a new internal tool, or are willing to port the admin classes you
  actually use (start with `manage.py vantage_adopt`);
- you accept a beta release, a smaller ecosystem and pinning an exact version.

They are not mutually exclusive during a migration: the stock admin (themed or not) can
stay mounted on another prefix while Vantage takes over model by model.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/settings/

# Settings

[← Index](index.md)

Everything a project owner can configure lives in a single `VANTAGE` dict in Django
settings.

```python
# settings.py
VANTAGE = {
    "SITE_TITLE": "Acme",
    "BRAND_COLOR": "#0ea5e9",
    "THEME": "system",
}
```

## Typos are errors

A key absent from the recognised set is a typo, and it is refused at once — both when a
setting is first read and by `manage.py check` (`vantage.E002`):

```pycon
>>> VANTAGE = {"SITE_TTLE": "Acme"}
ImproperlyConfigured: Unrecognised key(s) in the VANTAGE setting:
  'SITE_TTLE' is not a Vantage setting. Did you mean 'SITE_TITLE'?
```

Values with a fixed set of choices are checked too (`vantage.E003`):

```pycon
>>> VANTAGE = {"THEME": "sepia"}
ImproperlyConfigured: VANTAGE['THEME'] must be one of light, dark, system; got 'sepia'.
```

So are the two values rendered into every page's inline stylesheet, where a typo would
otherwise fail every render, the sign-in page included: `BRAND_COLOR` must be a hex
colour (`vantage.E004`) and `BRAND_RADIUS` a CSS length (`vantage.E005`), by the same
validators the settings screen applies to what it stores.

## Where a value comes from

```
SiteConfiguration row  >  settings.VANTAGE  >  built-in default
```

The database layer sits **underneath** attribute access rather than beside it, so every
existing read picks up a change made in the panel without knowing a database exists. It
is lazy (nothing touches the database at import or at `ready()`), failure-tolerant (a
missing table resolves silently to the file settings, which is what makes the migration
that creates the table possible to run), and cached per request.

Not every key can be changed from the UI — see
[what the settings screen deliberately cannot change](theming.md#what-it-deliberately-cannot-change).
The **UI** column below says which ones can.

## Branding

| Key | Default | UI | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SITE_TITLE` | `"Django Vantage"` | ✓ | Name in the sidebar, the page heading and the browser tab |
| `SITE_ACRONYM` | derived from `SITE_TITLE` | ✓ | Two-letter mark for the collapsed sidebar. `"Acme Corporation"` → `AC` |
| `LOGO` | `None` | ✓ | Static path or resolved URL, shown in the sidebar |
| `LOGO_DARK` | falls back to `LOGO` | ✓ | Used in the dark theme |
| `FAVICON` | `None` | ✓ | Browser tab icon |
| `BRAND_COLOR` | `"#6366f1"` | ✓ | The one colour the whole palette is derived from |
| `BRAND_RADIUS` | `"0.5rem"` | ✓ | `--radius`. Validated as a CSS length |
| `THEME` | `"system"` | ✓ | `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"` |
| `THEME_TOGGLE` | `True` | ✓ | Whether users may switch theme. `False` pins everyone to `THEME` |
| `UI_THEME` | `"vantage"` | ✓ | The look: a preset name. See [UI theme presets](ui-themes.md) |
| `UI_THEMES` | `{}` |  | Custom presets; omitted keys inherit from `vantage` |
| `UI_THEME_TOGGLE` | `True` | ✓ | Whether each person may choose their own preset |
| `CUSTOM_CSS` | `None` | — | A stylesheet loaded after Vantage's own |
| `LOGIN_IMAGE` | `None` | ✓ | Image beside the sign-in form, when you mount [Vantage's auth views](getting-started.md#signing-in) |

Details: [Theming](theming.md).

## Discovery

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTO_REGISTER` | `True` | Register every eligible model automatically |
| `EXCLUDE` | `[]` | App labels (`"sessions"`) or model labels (`"blog.Draft"`) to skip |
| `INCLUDE_ONLY` | `None` | When set, **only** these are registered and `EXCLUDE` is ignored |

Both accept app labels and model labels, matched case-insensitively.

```python
VANTAGE = {"EXCLUDE": ["django_celery_results", "blog.Draft"]}
```

Auto-registration always skips abstract models and auto-created M2M through-tables, plus
a fixed list of framework plumbing: `sessions.session`, `contenttypes.contenttype`,
`auth.permission`, `admin.logentry`, and Vantage's own tables. `auth.User` and
`auth.Group` are deliberately **not** on that list — they are among the most useful
things to administer.

Vantage's own models are excluded for reasons rather than tidiness: a generic CRUD form
over `SiteConfiguration` would route around the superuser gate on the settings screen,
an editable audit log is not an audit log, and a generic form over a saved view routes
around every permission rule the feature has.

Proxy models are kept: they are a normal way to give a model a second,
differently-configured presence in the panel.

Auto-registration runs **after** `panel.py` discovery and never clobbers an existing
registration.

## Navigation

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `NAV` | `None` | Declare the sidebar instead of deriving it |
| `NAV_UNLISTED` | `"append"` | What happens to registered models `NAV` does not mention: `"append"` or `"hide"` |
| `DASHBOARD` | `None` | Dotted path to a `Dashboard` subclass |

With `NAV` unset, navigation is **derived**: registering a model is enough to make it
reachable, grouped by app, with groups sorted by the lowest `order` of any panel in them
and items sorted alphabetically.

Setting `NAV` switches to **declared**:

```python
VANTAGE = {
    "NAV": [
        {"route": "vantage:dashboard", "label": "Overview", "icon": "layout-dashboard"},
        {"group": "Commerce", "items": [
            {"model": "shop.Order", "badge": "live"},
            {"model": "shop.Product", "label": "Catalogue"},
            "shop.Category",
        ]},
        {"group": "System", "items": [
            {"route": "vantage:settings", "label": "Settings", "icon": "sliders"},
            {"page": "schema", "label": "Schema", "icon": "share-2"},
        ]},
        {"group": "Elsewhere", "icon": "shield", "items": [
            {"url": "https://status.example.com", "label": "Status"},
        ]},
    ],
}
```

Each item needs exactly one of:

| Key | Points at |
|---|---|
| `model` | `"app_label.ModelName"`, matched case-insensitively |
| `page` | A registered page's slug |
| `route` | A URL name, with optional `args` |
| `url` | A literal URL; `external` is inferred from the scheme |

Plus optional `label`, `icon` and `badge`. A bare string is shorthand for
`{"model": "..."}`. A top-level item outside any group renders without a heading — the
usual shape for a Dashboard link. A group takes `group` (or `label`), `icon` and
`collapsed`.

Three properties:

**Declaring a nav can reorder, rename and hide — it can never grant access.** Every
entry still passes through the permission layer, so an entry for a model the user cannot
open does not render.

**Unmentioned models still appear** by default, so registering a new model never makes
it silently unreachable. Set `NAV_UNLISTED = "hide"` for a strict sidebar.

**A malformed entry raises; an unresolvable one does not.** A typo is something the
author wants to hear about, and `manage.py check` reports it at startup
(`vantage.E020`, `vantage.E021`, `vantage.W020`) rather than leaving it to a request.
But a sidebar that 500s because someone lost a permission is a poor trade for
strictness, so an item that cannot be shown is omitted.

## Behaviour

| Key | Default | UI | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PERMISSIONS` | `None` | — | Dotted path to a `PanelPermissions` subclass |
| `SETTINGS_PERMISSION` | `None` | — | Who may open the settings screen. `None` means superusers only |
| `LIST_PREFS_PERMISSION` | `None` | — | Who may save a list's preferences **for everyone**. `None` means superusers only |
| `ROLES_PERMISSION` | `None` | — | Who may open the [roles & permissions screen](roles.md). `None` means superusers only |
| `ACCESS_REVIEW_PERMISSION` | `None` | — | Who may open the [access review](access-review.md). `None` means superusers only |
| `BREAK_GLASS_PERMISSION` | `None` | — | Who may grant and approve [elevated access](access-review.md#elevated-access-break-glass). `None` means superusers only |
| `BREAK_GLASS_SELF_SERVICE` | `False` | — | Whether someone allowed to grant may activate their own request. `False` keeps the two-person rule |
| `BREAK_GLASS_MAX_MINUTES` | `60` | — | The longest one elevated-access grant may last |
| `READ_ONLY` | `False` | ✓ | `True`, or a string that doubles as the explanation shown to users |
| `NOTIFICATIONS` | `{}` | — | Slack, Teams and email channels for approvals, failed webhooks and failed jobs — see [Notifications](notifications.md) |
| `METRICS` | `False` | — | Serve Prometheus metrics at `_/metrics/` — see the [runbook](runbook.md#monitoring) |
| `METRICS_TOKEN` | `None` | — | Bearer token a scraper sends; `None` allows signed-in superusers only |
| `SLOW_REQUEST_MS` | `1000` | — | Log panel requests slower than this to `vantage.requests` (with `SlowRequestMiddleware`); `0` disables |
| `ROLE_MAPPING` | `{}` | — | Identity-provider groups to roles, applied at every SSO sign-in — see [Single sign-on](single-sign-on.md) |
| `UNMANAGED_READ_ONLY` | `False` | — | Make every `Meta.managed = False` model read-only unless its panel sets `read_only = False` — see [Read-only models](permissions.md#read-only-models-and-legacy-databases) |
| `ENVIRONMENT` | `None` | ✓ | A banner across the top of every page |
| `AUDIT_LOG` | `True` | — | Record what people do in the panel |
| `COMMAND_PALETTE` | `True` | ✓ | The ⌘K palette |
| `SENSITIVE_PATTERNS` | `None` | — | The words that mark a field as a secret. `None` is the built-in list; a list replaces it; `["...", "nhs_number"]` extends it — see [Sensitive fields](sensitive-fields.md#the-vocabulary) |
| `DEFAULT_PER_PAGE` | `50` | ✓ | Rows per list page, unless a panel sets `list_per_page` |
| `MAP_TILE_URL` | `None` | — | Opt-in raster tiles for the [map view](list-views.md#map), e.g. `"https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"`. Must contain `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}`. `None` draws a dependency-free SVG plot and fetches nothing |
| `RELATION_PICKER` | `"always"` | — | `"always"` or `"threshold"`. Whether a single-valued relation gets the searchable picker regardless of row count, or only above 50 — see [Relations and the search threshold](forms.md#relations-and-the-search-threshold) |
| `RICHTEXT_EDITOR` | `"html"` | — | `"html"` or `"markdown"`. The control for rich-text fields — see [Rich-text fields](rich-text.md) |
| `RICHTEXT_EXTRA_TAGS` | `[]` | — | Tags added to the rich-text sanitiser allowlist. Code-only |
| `RICHTEXT_EXTRA_ATTRIBUTES` | `{}` | — | Attributes added per tag, e.g. `{"td": ["colspan"]}`. Event handlers and `style` are refused. Code-only |
| `RICHTEXT_URL_SCHEMES` | `[]` | — | URL schemes added to `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `tel`. Code-only |
| `UPLOAD_ACTIVE_SUFFIXES` | `()` | — | Active-content extensions (`.svg`, `.html`, `.xml`, `.js`…) a plain `FileField` may accept, e.g. `[".svg"]`. Empty refuses them all; an accepted file is still scanned for script — see [Security](security.md#active-content-uploads) |
| `IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` | `5242880` (5 MiB) | — | Largest file the CSV importer will read |
| `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` | `5000` | — | Most rows the CSV importer will read |
| `EXPORT_BINARY_MAX_ROWS` | `100000` | — | Most rows an Excel or PDF export may carry. Over it the export is refused with HTTP 413 (never truncated); CSV, TSV and JSON are not capped. Excel's own ceiling is 1,048,575 data rows |

The login throttle, rate limits and upload ceiling are behaviour keys too, documented
with their defaults in [Security](security.md#installing-the-middleware) — see
[Two settings layers](security.md#two-settings-layers) for why their defaults live
there.

`SETTINGS_PERMISSION`, `LIST_PREFS_PERMISSION`, `ROLES_PERMISSION`,
`ACCESS_REVIEW_PERMISSION` and `BREAK_GLASS_PERMISSION` each accept a permission string
or a callable taking the request:

```python
VANTAGE = {
    "SETTINGS_PERMISSION": "vantage.change_siteconfiguration",
    "LIST_PREFS_PERMISSION": lambda request: request.user.groups.filter(name="ops").exists(),
}
```

None is editable from the UI. `SETTINGS_PERMISSION`, `ROLES_PERMISSION` and
`BREAK_GLASS_PERMISSION` in particular would be self-grants.

`READ_ONLY` is enforced in the permission layer, not in the views, so it covers every
write path including ones added later — and it is checked **before** the superuser
bypass. See [Read-only mode](permissions.md#read-only-mode).

## Two-factor sign-in

On offer to everyone, required of nobody, until you say otherwise — see
[Two-factor sign-in](two-factor.md).

| Key | Default | UI | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TWO_FACTOR` | `True` | — | Offer authenticator-app codes on the account page and ask for them at sign-in. `False` removes the feature, and stops asking anyone who had set it up |
| `TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED_SUPERUSERS` | `False` | — | Superusers may not use the panel until they have set it up |
| `TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED_ROLES` | `[]` | — | Role (`auth.Group`) names whose members must use it, e.g. `["Finance"]` |
| `TWO_FACTOR_ISSUER` | `None` | — | The name an authenticator app files the code under. `None` means `SITE_TITLE`. No colons |
| `TWO_FACTOR_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `5` | — | Wrong codes in a row before the account's second step locks |
| `TWO_FACTOR_LOCKOUT_SECONDS` | `300` | — | How long the first lock lasts; each lock in a row doubles it, up to a day |

None is editable from the UI: a requirement the people it binds could switch off is not
a requirement. A bad value is an error at `manage.py check` (`vantage.E095`, `E096`) and
at the first page render.

## Multi-tenancy

Off by default. Setting `TENANT_MODEL` is the only thing that turns any of it on — see
[Multi-tenancy](tenancy.md) for the full design (fail-closed checks, resolvers, the
middleware requirement, and how writes are protected, not only reads).

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `TENANT_MODEL` | `None` | The model every other registered model is scoped to, `"app_label.ModelName"`. Every model must either resolve a path to it or be declared exempt once this is set |
| `TENANT_RESOLVER` | `None` | Dotted path to a `TenantResolver` subclass or any callable taking a request. `None` means [`vantage.tenancy.UserAttributeResolver`](tenancy.md#choosing-a-resolver) |
| `TENANT_FIELD` | `"tenant"` | The attribute the default resolver reads off the user, and the conventional column name on tenant-owned models |
| `TENANT_SCOPE` | `{}` | `{"app.model": "lookup__path"}` for anything inference cannot see on its own, and `{"app.model": None}` for a model that is deliberately shared across every tenant |
| `TENANT_EXEMPT` | `[]` | Models every tenant shares — reference data, mostly |
| `TENANT_UNSCOPED` | `"deny"` | What happens to a registered model with no path to the tenant and no exemption. `"deny"` shows no rows and is a `manage.py check` error (`vantage.E060`); `"allow"` shows every tenant's rows and downgrades the check to a warning (`vantage.W060`) |

None of the six are editable from the panel's own UI, deliberately: a tenant boundary is
not a preference, and a signed-in user narrowing or widening it from inside the panel
would not be a boundary.

```python
VANTAGE = {"TENANT_MODEL": "accounts.Organisation"}

MIDDLEWARE = [
    ...,
    "django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware",
    "vantage.tenancy.TenantMiddleware",
]
```

`vantage.tenancy.TenantMiddleware` is not optional once `TENANT_MODEL` is set —
`manage.py check` refuses to pass without it (`vantage.E065`), because a resolver
without the request published to it fails closed rather than resolving nothing.

## Background jobs

A bulk action estimated at more than `JOB_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` of work is written as a
job row and worked off the request instead of run inline — see
[Background jobs](lists.md#background-jobs) for the routing rule, the chunking and
retry behaviour, and the backends it is tried against.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `JOBS` | `True` | Whether large bulk actions may be offloaded at all. `False` always runs in the request, whatever the estimate |
| `JOB_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` | `2.0` | The line between running in the request and writing a job row, in seconds of estimated work |
| `JOB_CHUNK_SIZE` | `500` | Rows per transaction while a job runs |
| `JOB_MAX_STORED_ERRORS` | `1000` | Most per-row errors kept for the downloadable report |
| `JOB_RETENTION_DAYS` | `30` | How long a finished job's row is kept before it is swept |
| `JOB_QUEUE` | `"default"` | Queue name passed to `django.tasks` or RQ. Celery uses its own routing instead |

## Webhooks

A POST to a URL you choose when a record is created, changed or deleted — see
[Webhooks](webhooks.md) for the payload, the signature and the retry rules. A malformed
value is `vantage.E100` (a switch that is not `True`/`False`) or `vantage.E101` (a limit
that is not a number above zero).

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `WEBHOOKS` | `True` | `False` fires nothing and hides the page. Stored webhooks are kept |
| `WEBHOOKS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` | `False` | Lets webhooks call loopback, private, link-local and other non-public addresses. Code-only, never editable in the panel |
| `WEBHOOKS_TIMEOUT` | `5` | Seconds a receiver may take per socket operation. A whole attempt gets three times this; the in-process fallback caps it at 3 in total |
| `WEBHOOKS_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `6` | Attempts before a delivery is marked failed, the first included |
| `WEBHOOKS_BACKOFF_SECONDS` | `30` | Wait before the first retry; each later wait doubles, up to a day |
| `WEBHOOKS_RETENTION_DAYS` | `30` | How long a finished delivery is kept before `manage.py vantage_webhooks` removes it |

## Scheduled reports

A saved view mailed as a CSV on a schedule — see [Scheduled reports](reports.md) for who
the export runs as, the size cap and the cron command. A malformed value is
`vantage.E115` (a switch that is not `True`/`False`), `vantage.E116` (a limit that is not a
number above zero) or `vantage.E117` (a base URL that does not start with `http://` or
`https://`).

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `REPORTS` | `True` | `False` sends nothing and hides the pages and the Subscribe control. Stored subscriptions are kept |
| `REPORTS_MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB` | `10` | Largest CSV attached to an email. A bigger report is sent as a short note, without the file |
| `REPORTS_MAX_PER_USER` | `25` | Subscriptions one person may hold |
| `REPORTS_RETENTION_DAYS` | `90` | How long a send log is kept before `manage.py vantage_reports` removes it |
| `REPORTS_BASE_URL` | `""` | Where links in report emails point, e.g. `"https://panel.example.com"`. Empty uses the address the subscription was made from, which comes from the request's `Host` header; set it in production (`vantage.W115`) |

## Undo

After a delete or an edit, the toast offers **Undo** for a few seconds — see
[Undo](undo.md) for what can be undone, and the cases in which the toast deliberately
has no button.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `UNDO_WINDOW` | `10` | Seconds the Undo button stays redeemable. `0` turns undo off everywhere |
| `UNDO_MAX_ROWS` | `1000` | Most rows one undo may carry, cascade included. Larger changes still happen, without Undo |

`ModelPanel.undo = False` turns it off for one model.

## Agents

Content-safety settings for anything handed to an AI agent; see
[Agent content safety](agent-content-safety.md).

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENT_MAX_FIELD_CHARS` | `2000` | Longest text value handed to an agent. Longer values are cut and end with a `[truncated]` marker |
| `AGENT_DEFAULT_ACCESS` | `"read"` | What agents may do with a model whose panel leaves `agent_access` unset: `"none"`, `"read"` or `"write"` |

Bearer-token access to the JSON API for non-human callers. See [Agents](agents.md).

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS` | `False` | Turns agent identities on. Off, every `Authorization: Bearer` request is a 401. Warns with `vantage.W116` in production without HTTPS |
| `AGENT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `60` | Requests per minute given to a new identity. `0` means no limit |
| `AGENT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | `[]` | Extra browser origins (for example `"https://tools.example.com"`) that may call the [MCP endpoint](mcp.md). Empty allows only the panel's own origin. Code-only |

## Scale

What a list page does once the table outgrows the sample data. Everything is fast at
200 rows; these keys are about the other end.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `LIST_COUNT_CAP` | `10000` | Rows counted exactly before the page reports `10,000+`. A page-depth budget, not a data limit |
| `LIST_COUNT_ESTIMATES` | `True` | Above the cap, replace `10,000+` with a planner estimate where one is available |
| `LIST_ESTIMATE_CACHE_SECONDS` | `300` | How long an estimate is cached |
| `LIST_KEYSET_THRESHOLD` | `50000` | Offset depth above which keyset paging is used. `0` disables it |
| `LIST_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` | `10000` | Per-statement ceiling for list-page queries. `0` disables it |

`COUNT(*)` on Postgres is always a full relation scan under MVCC, and it costs that
whether the page is showing 25 rows or two million. Details, and the reasoning behind
each number: [Deployment](deployment.md#counting-a-large-table).

## Data quality

One key, `DATA_QUALITY`, holding a dict of its own settings (`ENABLED`, `PERMISSION`,
`SAMPLE_SIZE`, `STALE_DAYS`, and so on). Unknown keys inside it are rejected like any
other typo. Every one is documented in [Data quality](data-quality.md#settings).

## Plugins

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `PLUGINS` | `None` | An allowlist. When set, only these plugins load |
| `PLUGINS_EXCLUDE` | `[]` | A denylist |

Both are matched against the entry-point name or the plugin's own `name`. Installing a
package must be reversible without uninstalling it, particularly when the reason for
turning it off is that it is broken. See [Extending](extending.md).

## The complete list

Every key in `vantage.conf.DEFAULTS`, and nothing else — `tests/test_release.py` fails
if the two drift apart:


## Reading a setting in your own code

```python
from vantage.conf import vantage_settings

vantage_settings.SITE_TITLE
```

Always through that object, never `settings.VANTAGE["SITE_TITLE"]` directly: this layer
supplies the defaults, derives values, applies the database overrides and rejects typos.
Asking for a key that is not a Vantage setting raises `AttributeError`.

The cache is invalidated by Django's `setting_changed` signal, so `override_settings`
works as expected in tests.

## Django settings that matter

| Setting | Why |
|---|---|
| `LOGIN_URL` | Where anonymous visitors are sent. Point it at [Vantage's auth views](getting-started.md#signing-in) or your own |
| `LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL` | Where they land afterwards |
| `MEDIA_ROOT` / `MEDIA_URL` | Required for logo uploads from the settings screen |
| `CACHES` | A dummy backend disables facet-count caching; the system page warns |
| `STATIC_ROOT` | `collectstatic` needs it in production |
| `LANGUAGE_CODE` | An RTL language flips the layout automatically |
| `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS` | Where django-guardian or django-rules is plugged in |
