URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/data-quality/

# Data quality

A read-only health check of the *rows* in every registered model, at
`/_/data-quality/` under the System group, and as `manage.py vantage_data_quality`.

`System` answers "is the deployment sound?". This answers the question that comes a
month later: is the data any good?

![The data quality overview](assets/screenshots/data-quality-light.webp){ .dv-shot .dv-only-light }
![The data quality overview](assets/screenshots/data-quality-dark.webp){ .dv-shot .dv-only-dark }

## What it checks

| Check | Finds | Links to the list page? |
|---|---|---|
| `nulls` | Share of rows where a nullable or blank field is empty | Yes, for nullable non-text fields the list filters on |
| `duplicates` | Fields named like identifiers (`email`, `slug`, `sku`, `code`, `username`...) that are not unique-constrained but hold repeated values (case-insensitive) | No |
| `orphans` | Foreign keys with `db_constraint=False` and generic foreign keys that point at a missing row or a missing content type | No |
| `choices` | Values outside the field's declared `choices` | No |
| `dates` | Created-like timestamps in the future (more than a day of clock skew) and any date before 1900 | Yes, as a date window |
| `empty` | A model with no rows | n/a |
| `stale` | A last-modified field (`auto_now`, `updated_at`, `modified`...) older than `STALE_DAYS` | Yes, as a date window |

A link is only offered when the list page can express exactly the offending rows: the
panel must filter on that field (`list_filter`, or inferred) and the real filter must
accept the value. Otherwise the finding has no link rather than a wrong one.

The overview lists every model with its row count, a 0-100 score and its worst issue;
click a model for field-level findings and how each check went. The score is 100 minus
25 per failure (an orphaned reference) and 8 per warning, per finding rather than per
row. Notes (a nullable field that is mostly filled, an empty table) cost nothing.

## It never shows a value

A finding is a count, a field name and a link. No cell from any row is ever read into
the report, so the page cannot become a way around field masking. That holds for the
page, the cache, the JSON output and the command.

## It is bounded

* Above `SAMPLE_SIZE` rows, checks read the **newest rows by primary key** (one index
  lookup finds the cutoff). The report says `sampled`, and findings say "in sample".
* Above `SKIP_ABOVE` *estimated* rows (PostgreSQL planner estimate; reuses the list
  page's `~` counts) the data checks are skipped and the row says `skipped`.
* Each check has `CHECK_TIME_BUDGET` seconds, enforced between queries and, on
  PostgreSQL, as a `statement_timeout`. A check that runs out keeps what it found and
  is marked `timeout`.
* A render spends at most `PAGE_TIME_BUDGET` seconds auditing. Models not reached show
  `not yet run`; the **Re-run** button continues where it stopped.
* Results are cached (`CACHE_SECONDS`). The key hashes the scoped SQL and the
  thresholds, so a different user, tenant or setting never sees someone else's result.

Background jobs were considered and not used: `vantage.jobs` is built around a stored
action and selection, and an audit has neither. For a very large database run the
management command from cron or CI; it has no page budget and warms the same cache the
page reads.

## Access

Superusers by default. Widen it with a permission string or a callable:

```python
VANTAGE = {
    "DATA_QUALITY": {
        "PERMISSION": "myapp.view_data_quality",   # or lambda request: ...
    },
}
```

Whoever gets in still only sees models the permission resolver lets them *view*, through
the same queryset as the list page: the panel's `get_queryset`, the resolver's
`filter_queryset` and tenant scoping. A tenant-scoped user audits their tenant's rows.

## Settings

All under `VANTAGE["DATA_QUALITY"]`; an unknown key is an error with a suggestion.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ENABLED` | `True` | `False` hides the page and disables the command |
| `PERMISSION` | `None` | `None` is superusers; a permission string or `callable(request)` |
| `CHECKS_EXCLUDE` | `[]` | Check names skipped everywhere |
| `SAMPLE_SIZE` | `50000` | Rows read per model before sampling |
| `SKIP_ABOVE` | `5000000` | Estimated rows above which data checks are skipped |
| `CHECK_TIME_BUDGET` | `3.0` | Seconds per check per model |
| `PAGE_TIME_BUDGET` | `12.0` | Seconds a page render may spend auditing |
| `CACHE_SECONDS` | `3600` | How long a result is cached |
| `NULL_WARN_RATE` | `0.5` | Empty share above which a field is a warning |
| `STALE_DAYS` | `365` | Days without a change before a table is stale |
| `DUPLICATE_FIELDS` | `[]` | Extra field names (`"external_id"` or `"app.model.field"`) to treat as should-be-unique |

## Opting a model out

One line on the panel:

```python
class AuditLogPanel(ModelPanel):
    data_quality = False                 # leave it out entirely
    # data_quality = ["nulls", "stale"]  # or skip just these checks
```

An unknown check name is `vantage.E063` in `manage.py check`.

## Adding a check

```python
from vantage.dataquality import Check, register_check

@register_check
class InvoicesHaveLines(Check):
    name = "invoice-lines"
    label = "Invoices without lines"

    def applies(self, panel):
        return panel.model._meta.label == "billing.Invoice"

    def run(self, ctx):
        # ctx.scan is the bounded queryset; ctx.tick() raises when the budget is spent.
        ctx.tick()
        count = ctx.scan.filter(lines__isnull=True).count()
        if count:
            yield ctx.finding(self.name, "warn", f"{count} invoices have no lines",
                              count=count, scanned=ctx.scanned)
```

Yield counts and field names only, never row values. `ctx.filter_url(path, value)`
returns a pre-filtered list link when the filter system can express it, else `None`.

## The command

```
manage.py vantage_data_quality [app.Model ...] [--format text|json]
                               [--fail-on warn|fail] [--no-cache] [--user NAME]
```

Runs as the first active superuser unless `--user` is given. `--fail-on` exits 1 when
any finding is at least that severe, for CI. Results are cached like the page's.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/webhooks/

# Webhooks

A webhook sends a signed `POST` to a URL you choose when a record is created, changed or
deleted in the panel, and keeps a log of every delivery. Open **System → Webhooks**.

```python
VANTAGE = {
    "WEBHOOKS_TIMEOUT": 5,        # seconds the receiver gets, per socket operation
    "WEBHOOKS_MAX_ATTEMPTS": 6,   # the first try included
}
```

Nothing needs configuring to start: add a webhook on the page, pick the models and
events it should hear about (none ticked means every model), and save. The **signing
secret** is generated for you and shown once, straight after saving. Copy it then; the
edit form never prints it again, and "generate a new secret" replaces it.

Who can manage webhooks: superusers, and anyone holding the `vantage.manage_webhooks`
permission. A hook can send every change to every model to an address of the manager's
choosing, so it is a permission of its own rather than something implied by editing a
model. `VANTAGE["READ_ONLY"]` blocks changing webhooks (the log stays readable).
`VANTAGE["WEBHOOKS"] = False` removes the feature; stored webhooks are kept.

## What fires a webhook

The same moments the [audit log](permissions.md) records: a create, an edit or a delete
made **through the panel** — the form views, inline edits, the JSON API's delete and
moves on a board. A soft delete (trash) is a `deleted` event with `"soft_delete": true`.
An edit that changed nothing sends nothing.

Out of scope, deliberately: changes made by `manage.py shell`, signals, imports and
other code, and bulk-action runs (which the audit log also records as one entry, not one
per row). A webhook fires whether or not `AUDIT_LOG` is on. The package's own tables
never fire one.

## The request

```http
POST /your/endpoint HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: django-vantage-webhooks
X-Vantage-Event: updated
X-Vantage-Delivery: 5b0c5c4e-6a0e-4f43-9a52-6c0b2f1f4e7a
X-Vantage-Timestamp: 1767225600
X-Vantage-Signature: sha256=3f1c…
```

```json
{
  "id": "0a1d5f06-8a64-4d4b-9f7b-2d9f0f7c3b11",
  "event": "updated",
  "model": "shop.order",
  "object_id": "1042",
  "object_repr": "Order #1042",
  "actor": {"id": 3, "username": "ada"},
  "timestamp": "2026-01-01T12:00:00+00:00",
  "changes": {"status": {"from": "draft", "to": "paid"}}
}
```

* `event` is `created`, `updated` or `deleted` (and `test`, from the **Send test**
  button). `id` identifies the event and is the same on every retry and redelivery, so a
  receiver can de-duplicate on it. `X-Vantage-Delivery` identifies one delivery.
* `changes` is `{"field": {"from": …, "to": …}}` for an edit, `to` only differing from
  null for a create, and `{"field": {"from": …}}` for a delete — the same shape as the
  audit log, including its rule that values are shortened and files are sent as names.
* `actor` is the person signed in, never the person being impersonated.

### Sensitive fields are never sent

Fields that [`sensitive_fields`](sensitive-fields.md) names or infers (passwords, tokens,
card numbers, ...) are removed from `changes` altogether — not masked, and not listed as
"changed" — and `object_repr` is the same safe label the audit log uses. A model whose
`__str__` is the secret should still not be sent to a third party; keep a webhook off it.

### Verifying the signature

The signature is an HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the secret, over the timestamp, a dot, and
the **raw body**. Including the timestamp lets you reject a replayed capture:

```python
import hashlib, hmac, time

def verify(secret: str, headers, raw_body: bytes, tolerance=300) -> bool:
    stamp = headers["X-Vantage-Timestamp"]
    if abs(time.time() - int(stamp)) > tolerance:
        return False
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(
        secret.encode(), stamp.encode() + b"." + raw_body, hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, headers["X-Vantage-Signature"])
```

Verify against the bytes you received, not a re-serialised copy. Every attempt is signed
afresh, so a retry carries a new timestamp.

## Where the work runs

Delivery never happens inside your database transaction. Each matching webhook gets a
delivery row, and the send is queued from `on_commit` through the same backend detection
as [background jobs](lists.md#background-jobs): `django.tasks` with a real queue, Celery
with a broker, or RQ. A Celery worker needs `vantage.webhooks` in its `imports`
alongside `vantage.jobs`.

**With no queue configured** the delivery runs in-process, right after the commit, with
a timeout capped at 3 seconds. This is a fallback, not the design: the request that
changed the record waits for the receiver. The webhooks page says so while it is true.

The wait is bounded as a whole, not only per socket operation: all the hooks one save
triggers share a **3 second budget**, and a hook that does not fit is left `pending` for
`manage.py vantage_webhooks` to send (after a couple of minutes) instead of making the
request wait longer. With many hooks, or a slow receiver, run a queue.

## Retries

A delivery succeeds on any `2xx`. Otherwise:

* network errors, timeouts, `5xx`, `408`, `425` and `429` are **retried** after
  `WEBHOOKS_BACKOFF_SECONDS`, doubling each time (30s, 60s, 2m, ... at most a day), up to
  `WEBHOOKS_MAX_ATTEMPTS` attempts in all;
* other `4xx`, any `3xx` (redirects are not followed), and a refused address **fail at
  once**.

Retries are scheduled with the backend where it can delay a task (Celery, RQ with a
scheduler, a `django.tasks` backend that supports it). Where it cannot — and always for
the in-process fallback, which must not sleep inside a request — the delivery waits as
`retrying` with a next-attempt time, and this command sends it when due:

```console
$ python manage.py vantage_webhooks      # from cron, every minute
Tried 3 due deliveries.
Removed 120 old deliveries.
```

It also picks up a delivery that was never queued (the broker was down) and removes
finished deliveries older than `WEBHOOKS_RETENTION_DAYS`; `--no-sweep` skips that.

## The delivery log

Each row records the status, response code, attempt count, how long the last attempt
took, the next attempt time, the error, and the first 2,000 characters of the response.
Open one to see the exact body that was sent. **Send test** sends a `test` event now, in
the page's own request, once, and reports the answer (it works on a paused webhook).
**Redeliver** queues a copy of the original body as a new delivery, with a new
`X-Vantage-Delivery` and the same event `id`.

## Safety

The URL is typed into a form and the *server* connects to it, so:

* **Private addresses are refused by default**: loopback, private ranges, link-local
  (including the cloud metadata address `169.254.169.254`), carrier-grade NAT, multicast
  and reserved ranges, and IPv6 forms that embed them (IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible,
  NAT64, 6to4, SIIT, and the old site-local `fec0::/10`). The check runs **at send time**
  on every address the host name resolves to — one bad record refuses the lot — and the
  connection is made to the address that was checked, not to the name, so DNS cannot
  change its answer in between. `WEBHOOKS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS = True` lifts it, for a
  receiver on your own network. It is a code-only setting for the same reason.
* **Redirects are never followed**; the `3xx` is recorded as the answer.
* **Proxy environment variables are ignored**, since a proxy would be connected to
  instead of the address checked.
* Only `http` and `https`, no credentials in the URL, a timeout on every socket
  operation, at most a few kilobytes of any response read, and a **total deadline** per
  attempt covering the name lookup, connect, send, headers and body: three times
  `WEBHOOKS_TIMEOUT` for a queued attempt, `WEBHOOKS_TIMEOUT` (at most 3 s) in-process. A
  receiver that sends a byte at a time cannot hold a worker or a request past it.
* Prefer `https`. The secret signs the body but does not encrypt it.

## Who can see what: hooks are global

Webhooks are not scoped to a tenant, a panel or a user's own permissions.

* A hook receives **every matching change to every model**, for every user and every
  tenant of the project, including models the person who made the hook cannot view.
* Anyone holding `vantage.manage_webhooks` (and every superuser) can create such a hook,
  point it at a URL they control, and **redeliver any logged payload to a new URL** from
  the delivery log.
* The payload is already stripped of sensitive fields, but the rest of `changes` and the
  record's label are sent as they are.

In a multi-tenant project treat `vantage.manage_webhooks` as equivalent to superuser:
grant it only to people who may read all tenants' data, and give no tenant admin the
webhooks page. There is no per-tenant filtering of hooks.

## Known limits

* The secret is stored in the database in the clear, because an HMAC cannot be computed
  from a hash. Treat read access to the table like read access to the secret.
* Delivery order is not guaranteed, and a retry can arrive after a later event.
  Use `object_id` plus `timestamp` if order matters.
* Delivery is at least once. De-duplicate on the payload's `id`.
* A response is stored truncated and as text; binary answers show as replacement
  characters.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/notifications/

# Notifications

Slack, Microsoft Teams and email for the events people otherwise miss: an approval
request nobody opened the panel to see, a webhook that has run out of retries, a
background job that failed.

```python
VANTAGE = {
    "NOTIFICATIONS": {
        "ops": {
            "type": "slack",                       # or "teams"
            "url": os.environ["SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"],
            "events": ["webhook.failed", "job.failed"],
        },
        "approvers": {
            "type": "email",
            "to": "approvers",                     # or a list of addresses
            "events": ["approval.requested"],
        },
    },
}
```

| Event | Sent when |
|---|---|
| `approval.requested` | Someone's edit was held for [approval](approvals.md) |
| `approval.approved`, `approval.rejected`, `approval.withdrawn` | The request was decided |
| `webhook.failed` | A [webhook](webhooks.md) delivery ran out of retries (test sends excluded) |
| `job.failed` | A [background job](deployment.md#large-bulk-actions-become-background-jobs) failed |

Channel keys: `type` (`slack`, `teams`, `email`), `events` (a non-empty list), `url`
(chat; an `https://` incoming-webhook URL — Teams accepts a Workflows or connector URL
that takes `{"text": ...}`), `to` (email; a list of addresses, or `"approvers"` for every
active user holding the model's `approve_<model>` permission, directly or through a role,
plus superusers). Anything else is rejected when the settings load.

## What a message contains

The event, the model, the record's label, the *number* of fields involved, and a link to
the record. Never a field value or field name: a chat channel's members may not be
allowed to see either. A webhook failure names the hook and the error; a job failure its
summary.

## Safety

- **Code-only.** Webhook URLs are credentials; keep them in your secret store.
- **Same network guard as webhooks.** Chat posts go through the webhook client, so
  private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused unless
  `WEBHOOKS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` is on, redirects are not followed and a post is cut
  off after 3 seconds.
- **After the commit, best effort.** Messages are sent once the database transaction
  commits, and a failing channel is logged to `vantage.notifications` instead of
  failing the save that caused it.
- **Global, like webhooks.** Channels receive events for every tenant. With
  `TENANT_MODEL` set, `"to": "approvers"` is refused (it would mail one tenant's record
  label to another tenant's approvers); list addresses explicitly instead.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/reports/

# Scheduled reports

Subscribe to a [saved view](lists.md#saved-views) and get it as a CSV by email every day,
week or month. Open a saved view on a list page and choose **Subscribe**; your reports
are under **System → My reports**.

```python
VANTAGE = {
    "REPORTS_MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB": 10,   # past this the email is a short note, no file
    "REPORTS_BASE_URL": "https://panel.example.com",
}
```

Nothing is sent until you run the sender. Put this in cron, every minute:

```console
$ python manage.py vantage_reports
Queued 2 due reports.
Removed 14 old send logs.
```

It also needs a working email setup: reports go out through Django's email backend
(`EMAIL_BACKEND` and `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL`, or `MAILERS` where your Django has it), the same way every
other message from your project does.

## Subscribing

Choose a saved view (a report is always a saved view: that is what gives it a name and a
filter) and **Subscribe**:

| | |
|---|---|
| How often | every day, every week (pick the weekday), or every month (pick the day) |
| Time | the time of day to send, in the site's time zone (`TIME_ZONE`) |
| Send to me | on by default; goes to the address on your account |
| Also send to | other addresses, comma separated. Only shown to people holding `vantage.send_reports_to_others` |

A monthly report on the 31st sends on the last day of shorter months. "08:00" stays 08:00
when the clocks change. The same form edits a subscription later, from **My reports**.

You can subscribe to a view you can open: the model's `view` permission and a view that is
yours or shared with you. Anyone with an email address can mail a view to themselves;
sending to anyone else is a permission of its own, because a mailbox is not necessarily
the person's. `REPORTS_MAX_PER_USER` limits how many one person may hold.

## Whose permissions the report runs with

**The export runs as the person who subscribed, with the rights they have when it
sends.** Not the ones they had when they subscribed: nothing about their access is stored,
the account is read from the database at send time, and the view is resolved by the same
code as the list page and its Export button. That means their model permission, their row
scoping, their tenant and the columns they have chosen for that list, and the same
masking: a sensitive column is exported as bullets, exactly as on the page.

A report is **skipped** and the reason recorded in the log, never sent, when:

* the account is inactive, or is no longer staff;
* two-factor sign-in is required of them (see [Two-factor](two-factor.md)) and they have
  not set it up, since the panel would make them enrol before showing them anything;
* the subscription was paused or deleted after a scheduled send had already been queued;
* they may no longer view the model;
* the saved view is no longer shared with them (or was made private);
* a filter in the view names a field that no longer exists. The list page shows a banner
  and carries on with more rows; an inbox has no banner, so the report is held back
  rather than silently widened;
* the model is no longer in the panel, the tenant has changed, or there is nobody left to
  send to.

Other addresses are checked the same way: they receive the report only while the
subscriber *still* holds `send_reports_to_others`. If they lost it, the report goes to the
subscriber alone and the log says the others were left out.

A skipped report keeps its schedule, so it sends again once access is restored.

**Send now** is an explicit request from the owner or a manager, so it still sends a
*paused* report; every other check above applies to it. It is refused in read-only mode,
like Pause and Resume, and each report can be sent this way at most once a minute: a
second click inside that minute is told how long to wait and queues nothing.

## The email

One message per recipient, so nobody learns who else receives it, with the CSV attached
and the number of rows in the body. Every message carries a link to the saved view in the
panel and an **unsubscribe** link, plus `List-Unsubscribe` headers for one-click
unsubscribe in mail clients.

**Size cap.** Above `REPORTS_MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB` of CSV (default 10) the file is not
attached. The email says how many rows there were, that the file was over the limit, and
points at the saved view, where Export has no such cap. The log marks the send as sent
without the file. Mind your mail provider's own limit, which is usually lower once the
attachment is encoded.

The links need the panel's address. `REPORTS_BASE_URL` sets it; without it the address the
subscription was made from is used. A subscription with neither is skipped rather than
sent without an unsubscribe link.

**Set `REPORTS_BASE_URL` in production.** The fallback address is read from the `Host`
header of the request that created the subscription, and a client chooses that header. If
the proxy in front of Django does not pin it (or `ALLOWED_HOSTS` is loose), whoever
subscribes can decide where every later email's unsubscribe and panel links point.
`manage.py check --deploy` warns about this as `vantage.W115`.

## Unsubscribing

The link is signed with `SECRET_KEY` and names one subscription. It needs no sign-in,
and all it can do is **pause** that subscription: the owner still sees it under My
reports, with the reason, and can resume it. Opening the link changes nothing (mail
scanners open every link); the page has a button, and mail clients' one-click `POST` does
the same. A link keeps working when `REPORTS` is off, and does not expire.

Rotating `SECRET_KEY` invalidates links in mail already sent, unless the old key is in
`SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`.

## The pages

**My reports** lists your subscriptions: schedule, next and last send, and a log of every
send with its status (queued, running, sent, skipped, failed), the row count, the
recipients reached, how long it took and the reason or error. Each row has **Send now**,
**Pause** or **Resume**, **Edit** and **Delete**.

**System → Scheduled reports** is the same for everyone's, for superusers and anyone
holding `vantage.manage_reports`. Managers can pause, resume, delete and send now. They
cannot edit: what is sent, and to whom, is the owner's, because the report runs as them.
**Send now** runs as the subscriber and sends to the subscriber's recipients, not to the
manager. It leaves the schedule alone.

`VANTAGE["READ_ONLY"]` blocks creating, editing, pausing and deleting. `VANTAGE["REPORTS"]
= False` hides the pages and the Subscribe control and stops sending; subscriptions and
logs are kept.

## How sending is scheduled

`manage.py vantage_reports` finds the active subscriptions whose time has come and
**claims** each one by moving its next time forward with a conditional update. Only the
process that changed the row queues a send, so running the command twice in the same
minute, or two cron hosts at once, sends once.

* A server that was down for a week sends **one** report when it returns, not seven. The
  next time is worked out from now.
* Each send then goes through the same backend detection as
  [background jobs](lists.md#background-jobs) and [webhooks](webhooks.md): `django.tasks`
  with a real queue, Celery with a broker, or RQ. A Celery worker needs `vantage.reports`
  in its `imports` alongside `vantage.jobs`. **With none**, the command sends the emails
  itself, one after another, and the pages say so.
* A queued send nobody picked up for five minutes is queued again; a run stuck "running"
  for an hour is closed as failed. Both are done by the command.
* Send logs older than `REPORTS_RETENTION_DAYS` are removed by the command;
  `--no-sweep` skips that.

Every minute is the right cadence for cron: a report goes out within a minute of its time.

## Settings

See [Settings](settings.md#scheduled-reports). A malformed value is `vantage.E115` (a
switch that is not `True`/`False`), `vantage.E116` (a limit that is not a number above
zero) or `vantage.E117` (a `REPORTS_BASE_URL` that does not start with `http://` or
`https://`).

## Permissions

| Permission | Allows |
|---|---|
| `vantage.manage_reports` | The System page: pause, resume, delete and send anyone's reports |
| `vantage.send_reports_to_others` | Naming addresses other than your own |

Superusers hold both.

## Known limits

* **CSV only**, with the columns the subscriber has on that list. No Excel or JSON.
* The CSV is built in memory up to the size cap, so a report is bounded by
  `REPORTS_MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB`; the rows are read in chunks and building stops as soon as
  the cap is passed.
* A text cell that begins with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading
  `'`, exactly as in the Export button, so a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of running
  it as a formula. Numbers, dates and booleans are not changed.
* A view whose list mode is a board or a map exports the table's columns.
* Deleting a saved view deletes the subscriptions to it.
* There is no per-recipient unsubscribe: the link pauses the subscription for everyone it
  goes to. The owner decides who is on it.
* Without a task backend, the emails are sent by the process that queued them, so the
  cron job (or, for Send now, the request) waits until they are out.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/accessibility/

# Accessibility

The target is **WCAG 2.2 Level AA**. This page says three things, in order of how much
they are worth: what the package guarantees and enforces in CI, what it needs from you
as a panel author, and what is still broken. The third list is the honest one, and it
is deliberately specific — a document that only lists successes is marketing.

---

## 1. What the package guarantees

Each of these is asserted by `tests/test_accessibility.py` against real rendered HTML,
not merely intended. If one regresses, the build fails.

| Guarantee | Criterion | Where |
|---|---|---|
| A skip link, first focusable element on every shell page, pointing at a real, focusable `<main>` | 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks | `base.html`, `vantage-auth.css` |
| Exactly one `<h1>` per page, and no heading level skipped | 1.3.1, 2.4.6 | every owned template |
| Every `<img>` carries an `alt` — `""` when decorative | 1.1.1 Non-text Content | all |
| Every form control has a `<label for>`, an `aria-label`, or a wrapping `<label>` | 1.3.1, 3.3.2 | all |
| Every button and link has an accessible name made of more than a glyph | 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | all |
| No positive `tabindex` anywhere | 2.4.3 Focus Order | all |
| Exactly one `<main>`; every `<nav>` carries a distinct `aria-label` | 1.3.6, 2.4.1 | `base.html` |
| `<html lang>` set from Django's active language; `dir="rtl"` when the language is bidi | 3.1.1 Language of Page | `base.html` and the auth pages |
| A visible focus ring on every focusable element, at ≥3:1 against its surface for **any** `BRAND_COLOR` hue | 1.4.11, 2.4.7 | `vantage.css`, swept in tests |
| `scroll-padding-block-start` so the sticky header never parks over the focused element | 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured | `vantage.css:25` |
| All animation suppressed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` | 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions | `vantage.css:89`, guarded by `test_stylesheets.py` |
| A persistent, always-present `aria-live="polite"` region for messages | 4.1.3 Status Messages | `base.html` (`#v-toasts`) |
| Message severity carried as text (`Success:`, `Error:`) and not only as the toast's edge colour | 1.4.1 Use of Colour | `base.html` |
| Cross-token contrast — muted text on cards, foreground on the sidebar, accent pairs — clears 4.5:1 in **both** themes | 1.4.3 Contrast | `theme.py`, asserted in tests |
| A hovered primary button keeps its label at ≥4.5:1 for every brand hue | 1.4.3 | swept in tests |
| Sign-in errors announced via `role="alert"`, with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` on the offending field | 3.3.1 Error Identification | `login.html`, `authviews._style_form` |
| A 403 says "not allowed" and never "not found" | 3.3.1, and plain honesty | `403.html` |
| Resizing a grid column, by drag or by keyboard, announces the column's name and its new width through the grid's own live region, debounced rather than sent on every keypress or drag frame | 4.1.3 Status Messages | `vantage-grid.js`, `tests/test_accessibility.py` |
| The relation picker's real `<select>` is `inert`, not merely `tabindex="-1"` plus `aria-hidden`, so it does not surface as a second, nameless combobox in the accessibility tree | 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | `combobox.js`, `tests/test_accessibility.py` |

On a phone the bulk-action bar becomes a non-modal bottom sheet and the sidebar a drawer;
both close on Escape and hand focus back, and the sheet is a `role="dialog"` only while it
is one. The list keeps its grid roles when its rows are laid out as cards. See
[Phones](phones.md).

### The live region, specifically

`#v-toasts` is rendered **unconditionally**, even with nothing in it. A live region
created in the same DOM mutation as its first message is not announced — assistive
technology has to have been observing the node beforehand. A container wrapped in
`{% if messages %}` looks correct, tests green, and announces nothing. It collapses to
zero height when empty, so it costs nothing to leave in place.

Script that needs to announce something should append into `#v-toasts`, or write into
it directly. Do not create a new live region per feature.

### The resize announcement, specifically

The resize handle genuinely changes a column's width in real time — the control was
always operable — but until this pass nothing told a screen reader user what it had
become, so the effect was invisible even though the cause was not. Two things matter
about the fix:

- **It is debounced, not sent per keypress or per drag frame.** A held arrow key
  repeats several times a second and a drag is dozens of `pointermove` events; a live
  region is not a log for a screen reader to keep up with. One announcement lands
  half a second after the width stops changing, however many keys or frames it took
  to get there.
- **The column's name rides with the number.** "240 pixels wide" on its own does not
  say which column, and a screen reader user resizing by keyboard is not looking at
  the header to remind themselves. The announcement is always "*Column* column, *N*
  pixels wide."

It reuses the grid's existing `[data-grid-live]` region — the same one column
move, visibility, pin, density and shortcut-preference changes already announce
through — rather than adding a second live region for one more feature, for the
reason `#v-toasts` gives above: one region, watched from boot, is the whole
mechanism this package uses for status messages.

### The relation picker's hidden `<select>`, specifically

The control the browser submits is a real `<select>`, moved out of sight and driven
by `combobox.js`'s type-to-search box in front of it (see that file's own header
comment). Hiding it used to mean `tabindex="-1"` plus `aria-hidden="true"` — kept
focusable on purpose, the old comment said, "so the browser can report a constraint
violation against it." That reasoning is a real one in the abstract and a genuine
platform conflict when it applies: the WAI-ARIA spec says `aria-hidden` must not be
used on a focusable element, and Chromium resolves that conflict in the element's
favour, not the attribute's — a select kept focusable this way stays in the
accessibility tree as a second, nameless combobox next to the one the script draws.
Confirmed live against the demo (an Order's `Customer` field) with Playwright's
accessibility snapshot: two `combobox` nodes where a screen reader user should find
one.

Investigating rather than picking a side of that trade-off first: the reason given
for keeping the select focusable does not hold for this widget as it stands.
`required` is the only HTML5 constraint a `<select>` can carry, and `combobox.js`
already moves it onto the visible `input` before the select is ever hidden
(`input.required = true; select.required = false;`); nothing calls
`select.setCustomValidity` anywhere in the file. By the time the select is hidden it
has no constraint left for a browser to need focus in order to report — the concern
was real when the comment was written and is not live today.

That makes `inert` the honest fix rather than a compromise between the two options:
it drops the element from the accessibility tree without the `aria-hidden` conflict,
because it also makes the element genuinely unfocusable — which costs nothing here,
precisely because nothing above still needs it focusable. Script access
(`.selected`, `.value`, adding an `<option>` for a value that arrived from the
search endpoint) is untouched, since `inert` blocks user interaction and focus, not
code. A browser old enough to lack `inert` (older than Chrome 102 / Firefox 112 /
Safari 15.5 — in line with the `fetch`/`AbortController`/`DOMParser` this file
already assumes without a fallback) falls back to the previous `tabindex="-1"` plus
`aria-hidden` shape, which is the known phantom-combobox behaviour rather than an
interactive select sitting in the tab order.

**The trade-off, spelled out rather than left implicit:** this fix depends on the
select never again being a control a browser needs to focus. If `required` were
ever left on the select instead of moved to the input, or a future change relied on
a native validation bubble against it, `inert` would silently swallow that too.
Nothing in `combobox.js` does either today, and the comment beside the `inert` line
is the tripwire for the day something wants to.

**A tooling note for whoever re-checks this next:** Playwright's own
`locator.ariaSnapshot()` (what the MCP `browser_snapshot` tool is built on) still
lists the select after this fix — it was verified, in this same session, to not
consult `inert` at all, on a page with nothing else wrong (a bare
`<select inert>` in a scratch page still shows up as a `combobox` under that API).
It does correctly drop `hidden`, `display: none` and `aria-hidden`, which is why it
caught the original bug in the first place. The claim above is verified instead
against Chromium's real accessibility tree — CDP's `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`,
reachable from a Playwright session via `page.context().newCDPSession(page)` — which
reports the select with `ignored: true, ignoredReasons: [{name: "inertElement"}]`.
That CDP tree is the one platform screen readers actually query; `ariaSnapshot()` is
not a reliable check for an `inert`-based fix specifically, and reading it naively
here would look like a regression that is not one.

### Colour is never the only signal

`--destructive` and `--warning` are used for **borders and fills, never for body
text**. Measured: `--destructive` against `--card` reaches only **3.56:1** in the dark
theme and `--warning` against `--card` only **2.97:1** in the light theme, both short
of AA. Every error message in the pages this package ships is `--foreground` text
inside a `--destructive` frame, with the word "failed" or the field name spelled out.

---

## 2. What the package asks of you

The panel renders your data and your labels. These are the parts it cannot check.

- **Write real `verbose_name`s.** Column headers, `<dt>` labels and form labels all come
  from them. `verbose_name="dt"` is an accessibility defect, not a style one.
- **Give every model a `__str__` that identifies the record.** It becomes the `<h1>` of
  the detail page and the text of every link to it. `Post object (7)` in a list of
  forty links is forty indistinguishable links.
- **`alt` text for anything you configure.** `LOGO` gets `alt="{{ SITE_TITLE }}"`
  automatically; `LOGIN_IMAGE` is treated as decorative and gets `alt=""`, so do not
  put information in it.
- **`BRAND_COLOR` is safe to choose freely.** `color.accessible_pair` moves the derived
  lightness until the foreground clears 4.5:1, for every hue on the circle. You cannot
  pick a colour that breaks button contrast. You *can* break it by hard-coding a colour
  in `CUSTOM_CSS`, which nothing here can see.
- **Custom pages inherit the shell but not its discipline.** If you ship a template for
  a `Page`, start at `<h2>` — `base.html` does not emit the `<h1>`, your page does, and
  two of them is the most common defect in a custom page.
- **Do not add a positive `tabindex`.** It reorders the whole document, not your widget.
- **Do not rely on a badge tone.** `render.py` colours choice values it recognises as
  states (`paid` green, `failed` red). The label is always rendered too — keep it that
  way in any custom cell renderer.

---

## 3. Keyboard map

| Key | Scope | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Tab` | document | Next focusable. The skip link is always first. |
| `Enter` (on the skip link) | document | Moves focus into `<main>`; `tabindex="-1"` is what makes focus actually land. |
| `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` | document | Opens the command palette. Advertised via `aria-keyshortcuts` on the search box. |
| `/` | document | Focuses the search box. **See the gap below.** |
| `Esc` | palette, drawers, menus | Closes one level. The invariant is "always one guaranteed-safe escape", not the specific key. |
| `↑` `↓` | palette | Moves through results. |
| `↵` | palette | Opens the highlighted result. |
| Arrow keys | data grid | Move between cells. The grid is **one tab stop** (roving `tabindex`): `Tab` enters it, `Tab` leaves it. |

There is currently **no user preference to turn single-key shortcuts off**, which is
what WCAG 2.1.4 asks for. See the gaps.

---

## 4. Known gaps

Ordered by how much they matter. Nothing here is disputed; what is not marked fixed is
simply not done. **Vantage does not claim WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.** The three AA
blockers the first audit named are fixed as of `0.1.0a1`, but the findings under
[Found elsewhere in the package](#found-elsewhere-in-the-package-not-fixed-here) and
the absence of any screen-reader pass both still stand between this package and that
claim.

### The three AA blockers from the first audit

1. **WCAG 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts — `/` is bound on `document`.**
   `static/vantage/vantage.js` registers a `keydown` listener on `document`. It skips
   text inputs, textareas and `isContentEditable` targets, and the grid's "Keyboard
   shortcuts" switch turns it off — which satisfies 2.1.4's first remedy ("turn off").
   It did not always: the grid stores the switch as JSON `false` and this listener used
   to compare against `"0"`, so switching shortcuts off silenced everything except `/`.
   The `e` shortcut in `vantage-inline.js` (table-scoped: it fires only when the row
   itself has focus) ignored the switch entirely. Both are fixed and pinned in a real
   browser by `tests/test_browser.py::TestShortcutsPreference`. What remains is
   hardening, not a failure: there is no **remappable keymap**, and the tag/
   `isContentEditable` check approximates scoping — a custom element or shadow root
   with its own keyboard handling is invisible to it. `⌘K` requires a modifier and is
   exempt throughout.

2. **Links with no accessible name in table cells — fixed.** The list grid, dashboard
   widgets and a detail page's related blocks link one cell per row to its record.
   When that cell's value was empty, `render.py`'s `EMPTY` em-dash was the link's
   entire content and a screen reader announced "link, dash". All three now render
   through `partials/cell_link.html`: the dash stays visible but is `aria-hidden`, and
   visually hidden text — "Open *record*" — names the destination. Pinned by
   `test_accessibility.py::TestEmptyCellLinks`.

3. **Form field boundaries — fixed.** `--input`, the border of every text field,
   select and drop zone, measured **1.27:1** against the light background and was
   translucent (`oklch(1 0 0 / 16%)`, so unmeasurable) in the dark theme — far under
   the 3:1 that 1.4.11 requires of a control boundary. Both themes now use an opaque
   value that clears 3:1 against every surface a field sits on, `muted` and `secondary`
   included, for every brand hue in the sweep:
   `test_accessibility.py::TestTokenContrast::test_a_form_field_boundary_clears_three_to_one`.
   The dark theme's `--border` is still translucent, but it is a decorative separator,
   not a control boundary; `test_decorative_borders_are_knowingly_excluded` records it.

Heading order on the list page was on this list in an earlier pass of this audit:
`partials/list_prefs.html`'s `<h3>` section titles had no `<h2>` above them. They now
sit under a wrapping `<h2 class="v-sr-only">` (`list_prefs.html:38`) — visually hidden,
since the rail already has a visible label, but present in the outline — confirmed by
rendering `/admin/<app>/<model>/` and walking the heading sequence live: `h1` → `h2`
→ `h3` × 6 → `h2` → `h3` × 3 → `h2` → `h2` → `h2`, no skip anywhere.

### Not yet verified

4. **The guard covers most, not all, of the pages this work owns.** `ALL_PAGES` in
   `tests/test_accessibility.py` was `login`, `logged_out`, `password_change`,
   `dashboard`, `detail`, a custom page, `403`, `404`, `500` when this gap was first
   written. It has since widened to include `list`, `add`, `delete` and `settings` too
   — confirmed by reading the fixture, not assumed. `import`, `audit` and `search` are
   still **not** in it. A one-off probe of those three found them clean on the
   mechanical checks above — but "clean when probed once" is not "guarded". Widening
   `ALL_PAGES` to cover them is the next unit of work.

5. **No screen-reader testing has been done.** Everything above is static analysis and
   parsed HTML. NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver have not been run against a single page.
   Announcement order, table navigation and the palette's combobox are unverified in
   practice.

6. **Focus behaviour after JS DOM replacement is unverified.** The grid, the inline
   editor and the palette all replace DOM. Whether focus survives has not been tested
   in a browser here.

7. **No automated axe/Lighthouse run in CI.** The Python guard catches structural
   defects; it cannot catch computed contrast, overlapping focus, or reflow at 320 px.

### Found elsewhere in the package, not fixed here

A full audit of the templates and scripts outside this work's scope turned up roughly
sixty findings. They are grouped by criterion below; line numbers were correct at the
time of the audit and those files are under active change, so treat them as pointers.

**1.4.1 Use of Colour — meaning carried by colour alone.** `partials/stat_card.html`
(`data-tone` on the value, and a trend direction whose hidden text says "versus the
preceding period" but never "up" or "down"); `partials/widget.html` (`<dd data-tone>`);
`partials/inline_cell.html` (the staged/saved/rejected dot is `aria-hidden` and coloured
only); `partials/saved_views.html` (locked and shared are icon + `title` on a span);
`partials/analytics.html` (legend swatch keyed by `data-index` colour);
`form.html` and `confirm_delete.html` (message severity is `data-tone` only);
`pages/schema.html` (`fk` and `o2o` edges differ only in stroke colour).

**4.1.3 Status Messages — changes nothing announces.** The selection count and the bulk
action bar in `list.html` / `vantage.js`; the peek-drawer load failure and loading
state in `vantage-grid.js`; the reorder result in `vantage-listprefs.js`; the
character counter in `vantage-editors.js`. (The contrast readout and warning in
`settings.html` were on this list in an earlier pass; `data-preview-ratio` now
carries `role="status" aria-live="polite"`, confirmed by reading the rendered
template, so both are covered by the guarantee above instead.)

**2.1.1 Keyboard — server HTML that is unusable without JavaScript.** `list.html` ships
`tabindex="-1"` in the template on the select-all box, every row checkbox, every sort
link and every primary cell link. With the grid script absent, the table cannot be
sorted, selected or opened by keyboard at all. The roving tabindex should be applied by
`vantage-grid.js` at boot, not baked into the response.

**4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.** `list.html` puts `role="tab"` on two plain navigation links
with no tabpanel; `audit.html` puts `role="search"` on a form with no search field;
`partials/grid_controls.html` puts `role="dialog"` on a non-modal popover with no focus
trap or restore; `vantage-editors.js` sets `role="toolbar"` without roving tabindex, and
sets `aria-controls` to a possibly-empty id; `pages/schema.html` puts `role="img"` on an
SVG containing focusable links.

**2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured.** Three sticky bottom elements — the summary `<tfoot>`, the
inline changeset bar and the form save bar — with only `scroll-padding-block-start` set
globally. A focused control at the foot of the viewport can be covered.

**Focus management.** `vantage-grid.js` rebuilds the columns list on toggle and drops
focus to `<body>`; light-dismissing the columns popover loses focus the same way; the
error summaries in `form.html`, `import_upload.html` and `import_map.html` carry
`tabindex="-1"` but nothing ever focuses them after a failed POST.

### Deliberately out of scope for now

8. **WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements is satisfied, and was checked.** No `draggable`
   attribute or `dragstart` handler exists anywhere in the package; both reorder
   surfaces ship pointer button alternatives (`vantage-grid.js`, `vantage-listprefs.js`)
   and the file drop zone keeps the real file input. This is recorded because "we never
   shipped drag" is the reason it passes, and adding drag later would silently break it.
9. **The 500 page cannot honour an explicit theme choice made in a cookie.** It reads
   `localStorage` only, because reading the cookie needs the request and the request
   is exactly what may be broken. It follows `prefers-color-scheme` otherwise.
10. **`lang` on the 500 page defaults to `en`** when rendered with no context, for the
    same reason.

---

## 5. Mounting the accessible auth pages

The panel's own sign-in, sign-out and password pages are what the guarantees above
apply to. A project-supplied `registration/login.html` is not covered by any of them.

```python
# urls.py
from django.urls import include, path
from vantage import site

urlpatterns = [
    path("accounts/", include("vantage.authviews")),   # login, logout, password_change
    path("admin/", site.urls),
]

handler403 = "vantage.authviews.permission_denied"
handler404 = "vantage.authviews.page_not_found"
handler500 = "vantage.authviews.server_error"
```

`vantage.authviews` declares no `app_name`, and its route names are Django's own
(`login`, `logout`, `password_change`), so `LOGIN_URL`, `redirect_to_login` and every
`{% url 'login' %}` already in a project keep working. It is a drop-in replacement for
`include("django.contrib.auth.urls")` for those three routes.

---

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/browser-tests/

# Browser tests

`tests/test_browser.py` drives a real Chromium, through
[Playwright](https://playwright.dev/python/), against every other test file's blind
spot: JavaScript. Django's test client — what the other ~3,400 tests use — parses HTML
but never runs a line of script, so client-side-only bugs are invisible to it. Three of
them already shipped this way: the bulk-action bar staying visible at zero selection
(a CSS specificity bug, correct markup the whole time), the top bar's settings screen
linking a stylesheet and a script that did not exist (two 404s a test client cannot
see, because it never fetches anything a `<script>` or `<link>` tag points at), and
focus not moving to the error summary after a failed save (a behaviour, not a
document, so nothing short of running the script would notice).

The module needs no demo project and no server you have to remember to start:
`pytest-django`'s `live_server` fixture boots a real HTTP server against the same
`tests.testapp` fixture models the rest of the suite uses, for the duration of each
test, and Playwright drives a browser against it. Self-contained and deterministic —
same as everything else in `tests/`.

## Running them

They are **not** part of a plain `uv run pytest` and do not need to be — install
Chromium and they run in place, wherever `tests/test_browser.py` sits in the suite:

```bash
uv sync --group dev --group browser
uv run playwright install chromium
uv run pytest -m browser
```

Without the `browser` group, or with it but no downloaded Chromium, the module skips
cleanly — at collection time if `playwright` itself is not installed, per test if it is
installed but `playwright install chromium` was never run. Either way, `uv run pytest`
(no `-m browser`) still collects the file and reports the skip; it never errors and
never silently vanishes from the run. A contributor who has not opted into the browser
group gets an unmodified, green suite.

CI runs them in their own job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `browser`), separate from
the main test matrix so that job's runners never need Chromium at all.

## What it covers

- Focus lands on `#v-form-summary` after a failed save — the fix in `vantage.js`'s
  `focusErrorSummary` that nothing else in the suite pins.
- No console errors and no failed requests (a missing static file is a failed request,
  and fails the build) on the dashboard, a list, a detail page, a form, the site
  settings screen, the top-bar arrangement screen, a delete confirmation, and the login
  page.
- No element carrying `hidden` computes to anything other than `display: none` on any
  of those same pages — the generalised form of the action-bar bug.
- The relation combobox: typing filters the list, arrows highlight a row, Enter
  commits it, a chip appears, and the real `<select>` — never replaced, only driven —
  ends up holding the value.
- The account menu: Enter opens it on the first item, the arrows move between items,
  Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
- The grid's roving tabindex: exactly one element is tabbable at rest and after arrow
  navigation, and the column-resize handle's Left/Right exception to that contract is
  scoped to itself, with Escape handing focus back to the row.
- Column pinning under `dir="rtl"`, against a table forced to genuinely overflow its
  container (not asserted from CSS source, from real `getBoundingClientRect()` values
  at several real scroll positions): the pinned column stays flush with the
  inline-start (right, under RTL) edge throughout.

## Why they are written the way they are

- **No arbitrary sleeps.** Every wait is on a condition — an element appearing, an
  attribute changing, a `page.wait_for_function` predicate, `networkidle` — never a
  fixed delay.
- **A fresh Chromium per test, not once for the module.** `live_server` requires
  transactional tests, so the database is flushed between tests; each one creates its
  own user and fixture rows. Playwright's sync API leaves a running event loop on
  whichever thread called `chromium.launch()`, which trips Django's async-safety guard
  for any ORM query issued afterwards on that thread — verified directly, not assumed.
  A session-scoped browser would poison every database-touching fixture from the
  second test onward. See the comment at the top of `tests/test_browser.py` for the
  full reasoning; the short version is that data fixtures are always a dependency *of*
  the Playwright fixtures, never requested alongside them in an order someone could
  reshuffle.
- **Cookie-based login, not the login form, for every test except the ones actually
  about the login page.** A session created directly through
  `django.contrib.sessions.backends.db.SessionStore` and handed to the browser as a
  cookie is faster than driving the form each time and does not make sixteen other
  tests brittle against the login template's markup.

URL: https://pythondeveloper6.github.io/django-vantage/benchmarks/

# Benchmarks

[← Index](index.md)

**Published numbers are pending.** This page explains how to measure; it deliberately
contains no results, because numbers from one machine say little about yours.

## What the script measures

`scripts/benchmark.py` fills the demo project's `Order` table with `--rows` rows in a
throwaway database, then times, through Django's test client (no network, no browser):

| Scenario | Request |
|---|---|
| list page | `/admin/shop/order/` |
| filtered list | `?status=paid` |
| search | `?q=...` |
| detail | one record in the middle of the table |
| export (csv) | the filtered list as CSV, fully consumed |
| JSON API list | `/admin/_/api/shop/order/` |

Each URL is requested a few times to warm up, then `--repeat` times for the measurement.
The report gives the median and 95th percentile in milliseconds, and the number of SQL
queries one request runs (the query count is usually the more stable number).

## Running it

From a checkout of the repository, with the development environment installed:

```bash
python scripts/benchmark.py --rows 2000          # a few seconds
python scripts/benchmark.py                       # 100,000 rows
python scripts/benchmark.py --format json > bench.json
```

By default the database is a temporary SQLite file that is deleted afterwards. For
PostgreSQL or MySQL, pass a URL for a **scratch database**; the script runs
`migrate` and inserts data there:

```bash
python scripts/benchmark.py --rows 100000 \
  --database-url postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/vantage_bench
```

`--settings` selects another settings module that installs the `shop` demo app.

## Reading the result

- Compare runs on the same machine, the same database and the same row count.
- A single process serving one client at a time; it says nothing about concurrency.
- The test client skips the web server, static files and the network.
- Your own models, filters and permission rules will differ from the demo's.

# FAQ

[← Index](index.md)

## How finished is this?

**Beta.** The version is `0.3.0b1`, the first beta, and the PyPI classifier is
`Development Status :: 4 - Beta`. Beta means the feature set is complete for the
package's scope and the settings and panel attributes classified *stable* are frozen;
it does not mean the package has had an outside review.

What that means in practice:

- **The behaviour is heavily tested.** More than 5,000 collected test cases across more
  than 80 modules, including
  query-count assertions, a hue sweep proving the contrast guarantee, and a round-trip
  test asserting that what the exporter writes the importer can read.
- **The API has a contract.** Every setting and panel attribute is classified as
  *stable* (frozen, changed only through a deprecation cycle) or *provisional* (new
  since the last release). See [API stability](api-stability.md). Pin an exact version
  (`django-vantage==0.3.0b1`) while it is pre-1.0, and run
  `manage.py vantage_upgrade_check` before upgrading.
- **Several features are declared but not wired up.** They are listed below rather than
  glossed over.

Use it on internal tools and back-offices. It has not yet been through an independent
security audit or a published large-deployment validation; read the
[security model](security.md) before exposing it to people you do not trust with the
data behind it.

## How is this different from `django.contrib.admin`?

Django's admin is remarkable for what it is, and it has not fundamentally changed in
twenty years. Vantage keeps what made it good — configuration in ordinary Python, next
to your models — and rebuilds the rest.

### What is genuinely different

**Inference, and per-attribute inference at that.** `contrib.admin` shows one column
(`__str__`) until you write `list_display`, and no filters or search until you write
those too. Vantage infers columns, filters, search, ordering, widgets and query
optimisation from the model, and overriding one of them leaves the others inferred.
That second half is the part that matters: in `contrib.admin` there is nothing to lose
by configuring, because nothing was inferred.

**Query cost is a designed property, not an afterthought.** `select_related` and
`prefetch_related` are derived from the columns the page renders, so a new column
cannot reintroduce an N+1. Facet counts fold into a single aggregate rather than one
correlated subquery per choice. Stats share an `aggregate()` call, partitioned by the
join they force so Django ticket #10060 cannot produce two wrong numbers. Analytics run
under a query budget and defer rather than degrade.

**Bulk selection is a predicate, not a list of ids.** "Select all 40,000 matching" costs
the same as selecting three, and the scope that was actually resolved is always
reported back — `contrib.admin` shipped a defect where `select_across` silently stayed
off and a destructive action applied to page one only.

**Analytics in the box.** Stat cards, charts and a per-column summary bar, all computed
over the filtered queryset in Python you declare rather than in a template override.

**Design.** Light, dark and system themes, RTL, a full palette derived from one brand
colour with WCAG AA guaranteed, a command palette, a schema map, a cascade-delete
preview that counts, an audit log, saved views, and a customisation rail that lets a
non-developer tune a list page without a deploy.

**Read-only mode and impersonation**, both enforced in the permission layer rather than
bolted onto views.

### What is deliberately the same

- Configuration is a Python class next to your models.
- `panel.py` is discovered exactly the way `admin.py` is.
- Permission codenames are Django's, resolved with `get_permission_codename`.
- Forms are real `ModelForm`s. Validation, `_post_clean`, `construct_instance` and
  unique checks are Django's, untouched — only the widget mapping is replaced.
- `search_fields` is accepted as an alias for `list_search`, and
  `has_<action>_permission` hooks work as you expect.
- Misconfiguration fails `manage.py check`.

### Can I run both at once?

Yes, and that is the honest way to evaluate a replacement. Mount `contrib.admin` where
it already is, mount Vantage somewhere else, and adopt your existing configuration:

```python
# project/panel.py
from vantage import site
from vantage.contrib.django_admin import adopt_admin_site

adopt_admin_site(site)
```

Every model registered with `contrib.admin` gets a Vantage panel carrying its columns,
filters, search fields, ordering, page size, form fields, actions and permission
methods. Nothing in `admin.py` changes.

Only what the admin actually *declared* is translated — an attribute left at its
`ModelAdmin` default stays unset on the panel, so Vantage's inference still runs.
Adopting an admin that only set `search_fields` should not cost you inferred columns,
filters and widgets everywhere else.

What did not come across is **reported per model** through `manage.py check`, rather
than silently dropped. A silent partial translation is worse than no translation: it
looks finished, and the missing half is discovered by a user who needed it. Details:
[Extending](extending.md).

## What it does not do

An honest list. Some of these are decisions; some are gaps.

### Not implemented

| | Notes |
|---|---|
| **`panel.permissions`** | Removed outright, not merely ignored. Setting it fails `manage.py check` (`vantage.E020`). Use `VANTAGE["PERMISSIONS"]` or the per-panel `has_*_permission` hooks — see [Panels](panels.md#removed-attributes) |
| **Full translation coverage** | `locale/` ships `en` (complete) and `ar` (complete Modern Standard Arabic, including all six plural forms; strings added later fall back to English until translated), for templates, Python and the JavaScript alike — see [Internationalization](internationalization.md) |

`inlines`, `row_actions`, `list_select_related`, `related_tabs`, `layout`, background
job offload for bulk actions and per-field widget overrides (`formfield_overrides`,
`widgets`) used to belong on this table and no longer do — all seven are real, tested
features now. See [Editable inlines](forms.md#editable-inlines),
[Row actions](panels.md#row-actions), [The record page](forms.md#the-record-page),
[The layout DSL](forms.md#the-layout-dsl), [Bulk actions](lists.md#bulk-actions) and
[Overriding a widget](forms.md#overriding-a-widget).

**The JSON API is built.** [`vantage.api`](api.md) is a full read/write API over every
registered panel — cursor pagination, optimistic concurrency, the same permission and
validation path the HTML pages use. It has no file-upload endpoint (a JSON body cannot
carry binary data) and no bulk-action, saved-view or import/export endpoints yet; see
[what it does not do](api.md#what-this-api-does-not-do) for the current edge.

### Deliberately not done

| | Why |
|---|---|
| **Authentication itself** | Vantage ships *styled* sign-in, sign-out and change-password views over `django.contrib.auth`'s own forms, and no more. Password reset, MFA and SSO are the auth stack's job |
| **Row history** | Vantage's audit log records what a *person did in the panel*. Row history means a model and a migration in **your** app and roughly double the write volume; django-simple-history is the right tool, and it is soft-detected and rendered alongside when you have chosen it |
| **`raw_id_fields`, `autocomplete_fields`, `filter_horizontal` / `filter_vertical`** | The relation widget already searches above 50 rows. These are three names for one behaviour |
| **`prepopulated_fields`** | Slug prepopulation |
| **`save_as`, `save_on_top`, `actions_on_top` / `actions_on_bottom`** | Chrome placement is fixed |
| **Search prefixes `^`, `=`, `@`** | Every path is `icontains`. A prefix in a path is stripped |
| **Auto-enabling django-guardian** | Whether object permissions narrow the admin is a policy decision, not a consequence of having a package installed. Set `PERMISSIONS` explicitly |
| **A CSS or JS build step** | Assets ship prebuilt. No Node.js, no bundler, no htmx, no Tailwind — the CSS is hand-written OKLCH tokens and the JavaScript is dependency-free |

### Known limitations

- **Row counts above 10,000 are capped or estimated.** That is deliberate — see
  [counting a large table](deployment.md#counting-a-large-table) — but it means the
  number at the foot of a large list is `10,000+` or `~2,300,000`, not an exact figure.
  Planner estimates are Postgres-only and are withheld from row-restricted users.
- **A strict CSP needs one context processor.** The token stylesheet and the no-flash
  script are inline in `<head>`; `base.html` nonces both through `csp_nonce_attr` once
  `vantage.security.csp_context` is in your context processors, and `vantage.W056`
  warns if a policy is configured without it. A handful of inline `style` attributes
  remain, which no nonce can cover — see
  [Content-Security-Policy](security.md#content-security-policy) for the exact policy.
- **The import wizard stashes the uploaded file on local disk.** Running more than one
  process needs sticky sessions or a shared filesystem between the preview and the
  commit.
- **Multiple sites share one settings dict.** Branding, `NAV` and the permission
  resolver are global.
- **A tree spanning pages** shows a child whose parent is on another page as a root. That
  is the honest answer rather than a recursive lookup per row, but it can look odd.

## Does it need Node.js?

No. There is no build step, no bundler and no JavaScript dependency. The CSS is
hand-written using OKLCH tokens, the JavaScript is plain and dependency-free, and both
ship in the wheel. `collectstatic` is the whole deployment story for assets.

## Does it need a database table?

It creates four (plus one for background jobs), for site configuration, the audit log,
saved views and per-list preferences. Each is optional in practice: if the table is
missing, the layer that uses it silently falls back to what the code says. That is not
laziness — a settings layer that raises when its own table is absent makes the migration
that would create the table impossible to run.

## Which optional packages does it use?

All soft-detected, none required:

| Package | Used for |
|---|---|
| django-guardian | Bulk row scoping, via `GuardianPermissions` |
| django-rules | Object-level predicates, through `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS` |
| django-mptt | Tree detection |
| django-treebeard | Tree detection (MP, NS and AL node types) |
| django-simple-history | A row-history timeline beside the audit log |
| django-ordered-model | Sortable detection |
| Celery / RQ / Django Tasks | Reported on the system page |

Detection uses `apps.is_installed`, not `try: import`. A package being importable says
nothing about whether *this project* uses it, and importing an optional dependency is a
side effect that pure detection has no business having.

## Why is my column not showing?

In order of likelihood:

1. It is a `TextField`, `JSONField`, `BinaryField` or `FileField` — never a column.
2. Its name matches the [sensitive pattern](inference.md#the-sensitive-name-exclusion) —
   anything containing `password`, `token`, `secret`, `hash` and so on as a whole word.
3. It is a `CharField` longer than 200 characters.
4. It scored below the top six. Run `manage.py vantage_scaffold <app>` to see the
   result, then write `list_display` yourself.
5. Somebody hid it from the [customisation rail](lists.md#the-customisation-rail). A
   personal preference beats your `panel.py`; check whether the list has a site-wide
   preference row.

## Why is my filter doing nothing?

- The field is not in `list_filter`. Only declared or inferred filters read the query
  string.
- The value did not clean, so it was dropped. A filter rail is not a form, and a stale
  bookmark should degrade to a broader result set rather than to a 500.
- The path is partial — `created_at__year` is rejected rather than guessed at.
- The field type has no filter: text, JSON, binary and file fields belong in search.

## Why has my stat got no trend?

`trend` names a date field, and the previous period is computed from the span of the
data on screen. If the user has filtered *on that same date field*, the preceding period
has been filtered away. The list page passes a baseline queryset with that one filter
removed to cover exactly this, so if you are seeing it, you are probably calling
`compute_stats` yourself without a `baseline`.

## Why are two of my numbers wrong?

Almost certainly two aggregates over different multi-valued relations in one
`aggregate()` call — the joins multiply and **both** numbers are inflated, including
aggregates over local columns, which is the part that surprises people (Django ticket
#10060).

Vantage partitions stats by the join they force so this cannot happen across separate
stats, and refuses a *single* stat that reaches across two:

```
Stat 'Total' aggregates across the multi-valued relations ['items', 'reviews'] in one
expression. … Express one of them as a correlated Subquery instead.
```

If you are seeing wrong numbers anyway, check the summary bar: it only ever aggregates
local concrete columns, so a custom `list_aggregates` naming a traversed path is the
other place to look.

## Can a saved view or a stored preference show someone more than they should see?

No, and both are built so that the answer cannot become yes.

A saved view stores **query parameters**, and the rows are filtered by
`filter_queryset` on every request regardless of who saved it. URL filter state has zero
security value; a view decides only which of the rows you may already see are worth
showing you.

A stored list preference is validated against what the panel *currently* exposes, both
when it is written and again when it is read. It can hide, reorder and re-aggregate what
the panel already offers; it can never widen it.

## How do I contribute or report a bug?

```bash
uv sync --all-groups
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check src tests
```

The demo project in `example/` is the fastest way to reproduce something:

```bash
./example/run.sh          # migrate, seed, serve on :8765
```

# Roadmap

Everything that was on this page is built and waiting for the next release. Each item
links to its documentation, and the [changelog](https://github.com/Pythondeveloper6/django-vantage/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
lists the details and the known limitations. Ideas and use cases for what comes after
are welcome in the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/Pythondeveloper6/django-vantage/issues).

## In the next release

### Records

**[History with point-in-time restore](history.md).** See a record exactly as it was on
a given date, rebuilt from the [audit log](permissions.md#the-audit-log), and restore
some or all of its fields from there.

**[Approval workflows](approvals.md).** Mark fields that need a second pair of eyes:

```python
requires_approval = ["price", "status"]
```

A change to one of them waits for someone with permission to approve it before it is
saved.

### Access and security

**[Two-factor sign-in](two-factor.md).** Authenticator-app codes (TOTP), which you can
require for superusers or for chosen [roles](roles.md).

**[Field-level permissions](field-permissions.md).** "Support can see `price` but not
change it", set in the roles matrix next to the model permissions, and enforced on every
page, export and the JSON API, the same way [sensitive fields](sensitive-fields.md) are.

### Getting data out

**[Scheduled reports](reports.md).** Subscribe to a [saved view](lists.md#saved-views)
and get it as a CSV by email every day, week or month.

**[Webhooks](webhooks.md).** Send a signed POST to a URL you choose when a record is
created, changed or deleted, with a delivery log and automatic retries.

### Everywhere

**[A layout for phones](phones.md).** Lists become cards on small screens, and bulk
actions move to a bottom sheet, so the panel is usable away from a desk.
